requirement: When a DefaultIntervalCategoryDataset is constructed with non-null but zero-series start/end arrays (e.g. empty double[][]/Number[][] data), the constructor stores its series-keys and category-keys as zero-length (empty) arrays rather than as null, so that the key/lookup accessors that read those arrays operate normally instead of throwing: getRowCount() and getColumnCount() return 0, getSeriesIndex()/getRowIndex() and getCategoryIndex()/getColumnIndex() return -1 for any argument, and getRowKeys()/getColumnKeys() return (an) empty list rather than raising a NullPointerException.

For a horizontal-oriented plot, drawing a data item whose mean value (dataset.getMeanValue(row, column)) is null completes without throwing a NullPointerException: the item returns early, drawing no bar, no standard-deviation/error-indicator lines, and no item label for that item.

In Axis.drawLabel, when plotState is non-null and the label's hotspot has been computed (non-null), but plotState.getOwner() returns null, the method does not throw a NullPointerException; it skips the axis-label entity registration and returns the axis state normally.

After data items are added to a TimePeriodValues series (via add), getMaxMiddleIndex() returns the index of the item whose period's middle instant (= start + (end-start)/2) is the greatest among all held items: adding an item whose middle is less than or equal to the current maximum does not update maxMiddleIndex, even when that item's middle is greater than the current minimum-middle item's middle.

DefaultParser short-option recognition now matches a token against the FULL option name (the substring after a single leading '-', up to any '=' that separates an inline '=value') rather than only checking that the first character after '-' is a registered short option; consequently a token such as '-t1' or '-name=value' whose entire name is a registered (possibly multi-character) short/opt-name option is classified as an option.
The mayBeString(Node, boolean) non-recursive path (recurse=false), which delegates directly to mayBeStringHelper, is left unchanged by the fix.

JSDoc type-annotation alias expansion (e.g. rewriting an alias base name such as 'sub.C' to its expanded target) is applied to each goog.scope body's own original annotations independently of any injected ($jscomp.scope) copies that were produced earlier within the same or a previous goog.scope block; tracking used to deduplicate the jsdoc processing of injected declarations is cleared when leaving each top-level goog.scope scope rather than persisting across distinct goog.scope blocks.

In a function type clause of the form `this:` or `new:`, the context type may now be any basic type expression (e.g. array type, record/`{...}` type, union/`(...)` type, nested function type, `null`, `undefined`, or `*`), rather than being restricted to a plain type name; previously such context types caused the function type to fail with a generic type-syntax error.

When a function declaration inside a goog.scope body is rewritten, the original named 'function <name>(){}' statement is replaced: the function's name child is removed (made anonymous, to avoid an IE global-name leak) and the resulting anonymous function expression is emitted as the value of the generated '$jscomp.scope.<name>' declaration, replacing the prior location of the function declaration in the output.

GlobalNamespace's namespace builder treats a NAME node that is the parameter of a CATCH clause (i.e. catch (e) {...}) as a set/redefinition of that name: the reference is recorded as a SET_FROM_GLOBAL set (in global scope) or a SET_FROM_LOCAL set (in a local scope), with the name's type recorded as OTHER, instead of being classified and recorded as a read/get of the name.

ReferenceCollection.isAssignedOnceInLifetime now returns false (previously true) when, walking outward from the variable's sole assignment reference, a function basic-block is reached before any loop and that function's scope differs from the scope of the variable's declaring symbol; i.e. an assignment placed inside an inner/nested function scope capturing the variable is treated like an assignment that can execute more than once, not as an assignment occurring exactly once in the variable's lifetime, even though only one assignment statement exists and no enclosing loop is present.

CollapseProperties.inlineAliases does not treat a global qualified name declared in the externs (name.inExterns == true) as an alias-inlining candidate, even when it otherwise satisfies condition (b) (exactly one global set, no local sets, more than zero aliasing gets); consequently CollapseProperties leaves local aliases/references that read or alias such extern-declared names unmodified (not inlined, not rewritten to flattened names, not nulled out).
FunctionType.hasOwnProperty("prototype") returns true: a function type reports that it owns a property named "prototype" (in addition to whatever the superclass reports).

When Compiler.init(JSSourceFile[] externs, JSModule[] modules, CompilerOptions) runs with an input array of length >= 2, every module at array index >= 1 (i.e., all but the first/root module) whose input list is empty becomes, by the time init completes, non-empty: a single synthetic source input is added to it whose source-file name is '[' + <module name> + ']' and whose source code is the empty string (so it contributes no code on its own), and that added input is included in the compiler's aggregate input set (rebuildInputsFromModules/getAllInputsFromModules and the parsed inputs).

During reference collection within a scope, a NAME token whose string equals "arguments" is resolved to that scope's arguments Var (Scope.getArgumentsVar()) rather than to an ordinary declared variable looked up by name, so that occurrences of the bare identifier `arguments` (which is never an explicitly declared local variable) produce collected references keyed under the scope's arguments Var.

While collapsing a global name's declaration, the pass only emits separate flattened global variable declarations for the name's object-literal child values and emits stub variable declarations for the name's not-yet-declared (locally-set) child properties when the name's child property names can themselves be collapsed. When the child property names cannot be collapsed, the declaration of a collapsible name is updated without creating such per-child variables or stubs — an object-literal rvalue's keys are left inline in the kept object literal, and no stub vars are inserted for the name's children.

When NameAnalyzer's FindDeclarationsAndSetters visits a class-defining call (a CALL that touches class definitions, e.g. detected via CodingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall/ getSingletonGetter), it records that CALL as a removable ClassDefiningFunctionNode associated with the subclass name it defines, even when that subclass name has no other prior declaration/occurrence in the program and is otherwise unknown to the analyzer — thereby also creating such a name. (Previously a CALL whose defined subclass name was not already in the analyzer's symbol table was not recorded at all and thus never became a removal candidate.)

An object literal annotated with @lends whose lent name only becomes resolvable after the literal itself has been visited during traversal (i.e. the literal is not analyzed when first encountered, but only once traversal reaches the root of the statement containing it) must have its lent type resolved correctly and its properties defined onto that lent type, rather than being typed prematurely with an unresolvable/incorrect @lends type.

NodeUtil.functionCallHasSideEffects returns false (no side effects) for a CALL node whose callee is a GETPROP whose object is a single NAME whose string equals "Math" (i.e. a direct call of the form Math.<member>(...)), regardless of whether a compiler is supplied and regardless of the hasRegExpGlobalReferences condition.

Restricting an object type on the knowledge that its typeof result equals "function" (true condition) narrows the type to its callable/constructable sub-region (the greatest subtype of the object type within the function/constructor types): an object type that is itself already a function value is preserved as that function (non-null) rather than eliminated just because it does not wholly contain the generic constructor type, and a broad object supertype narrows to the generic function/constructor type.

In CheckAccessControls.checkPropertyVisibility, any node of the form `getprop` that is the assignment target of an ASSIGN node whose first child is that `getprop` is classified as an attempted override of the property (driving the override code path: PRIVATE_OVERRIDE reported when it overrides a @private property declared in a different input file, and VISIBILITY_MISMATCH reported when the override's own declared visibility differs from the overridden property's) if and only if that ASSIGN node carries JSDoc information (parent.getJSDocInfo() != null); being in the global scope is neither necessary nor sufficient for that classification.

RenameLabels run with removeUnused=false preserves (renames to its generated name) every explicit label in the traversed tree, including labels that are not referenced by any break or continue; it does not remove or delete the labeled statements in that mode. Unreferenced-label removal only occurs when removeUnused=true (the default mode, whose behavior is unchanged).

When CodeGenerator escapes a string/regexp with no output CharsetEncoder configured (default printing), a character whose code point is exactly 0x7f (DEL, U+007F) is not appended literally: it is instead emitted in its \u hex JavaScript representation (\u007f).

NodeUtil.isStrWhiteSpaceChar returns TernaryValue.UNKNOWN (no longer TernaryValue.TRUE) for the vertical-tab character (\u000B / VT), i.e. VT is no longer classified as definitively trimmable whitespace.

Dead assignment elimination no longer treats an assignment `v = RHS` (to a local variable `v`) as an unconditional kill of `v` when the assignment lies to the right of another value-producing assignment to `v` within the same expression: if `RHS`'s first reference to `v` is a read (a read occurring before any write to `v` within `RHS`), the live-ness scan reports a READ for that assignment instead of a KILL, so the earlier assignment to `v` is preserved (not eliminated) because its value is observable through that RHS read. Observable case: `if ((a=1)&&(b=a))` keeps `a=1`, and `return (x=1) && (x=f(x))` keeps `x=1`.

When ProcessCommonJSModules computes the module name for a script node in visitScript, it passes the raw source file name to guessCJSModuleName, which performs the (single) prefix-strip normalization internally; the earlier redundant outer normalizeSourceName call is gone. Because normalizeSourceName removes the configured filename prefix only once, a file whose path contains the configured prefix text again after the leading occurrence now keeps that later occurrence (and the filename prefix is stripped exactly once rather than twice), affecting the resulting module identifier.

When validating a function's @this type for the THIS_TYPE_NON_OBJECT check ('@this type of a function must be an object'), null and undefined are stripped from the given type before testing whether it is a subtype of Object, so a @this type that contains null/undefined alongside an actual object type (e.g. an optional/nullable type) is accepted (no JSC_THIS_TYPE_NON_OBJECT warning is reported), and the warning is reported only if the @this type's value portion after removing null/undefined is still not an object subtype.

CheckGlobalThis's lent-function exemption described above fires only when the @lends lend-name ends with '.prototype'; a function that is an object-literal property of an object literal carrying any other @lends annotation (or none, or a lend-name not ending in '.prototype') is still traversed and remains subject to GLOBAL_THIS reporting for its `this` uses as before.

Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int), when invoked with a non-null b, valid offset/len, and len > 0, never returns 0 to its caller so long as more input remains to be transformed: whenever processing the buffered chunk yields zero decoded/encoded output bytes yet (because the pending input has not yet formed a complete decoded/encoded group), the method keeps reading and processing further bytes from the wrapped InputStream and returns a positive count only once at least one transformed byte is available, returning -1 only at genuine end-of-stream. Consequently the intermediate 0 that the inner readResults call can produce prior to EOF is never propagated out of this method.

A MultiValueMap instance is an instanceof java.io.Serializable (the class now implements Serializable and declares a serialVersionUID), so mapping it to a plain serialization operation is no longer rejected for the map's own lack of serializability.

Calling close() while the current entry's written byte count does not equal the entry's declared size (e.g. an entry left partially/unwritten) now throws an IOException describing the invalid entry size, rather than silently closing the underlying stream.

After getNextArEntry returns an entry, calls to read(), read(byte[]), and read(byte[],int,int) on the stream return at most the remaining unread portion of the current entry's declared content length; a read attempted at or beyond the end of the current entry's declared content returns -1 (EOF). Consequently bytes belonging to the archive's subsequent header/padding are never surfaced through the entry-content read path.

When serializing a bitset whose length (number of entries) is a positive multiple of 8 — i.e. the bits exactly fill whole 8-bit groups — SevenZOutputFile's bit serialization writes exactly length/8 bytes and does not emit an extra trailing byte for the final, already-full byte group.

When TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders scans a PAX header for the decimal length of a record, a newline ('\n') byte encountered where length digits would otherwise be accumulated is treated as a blank/stray line that is skipped without contributing to the parsed length; parsing then resumes at the start of the next record, so that all valid `length keyword=value\n` records still populate the returned Map even when blank lines intervene in the header stream (instead of the newline being folded into the length, which yields a corrupt/negative length and garbled results).

After reading the next local file header signature from a non-first entry (or the shifted first header), if that signature is neither the Local File Header signature (LFH), the Central File Header signature (CFH) nor the Archive Extra Data signature (AED), getNextZipEntry throws a java.util.zip.ZipException whose message contains the offending signature value formatted as '0X%X' (hex), instead of returning null.

Each Date-based setter (setModifyJavaTime, setAccessJavaTime, setCreateJavaTime) throws IllegalArgumentException when the supplied Date's seconds-since-epoch value (its millis / 1000) falls outside the signed 32-bit integer range (i.e., is < Integer.MIN_VALUE or > Integer.MAX_VALUE); a value within that range is accepted without throwing.

In the DEFLATE read path, when the underlying Inflater has completed (inflate returns 0 and inf.finished() is true), read(byte[],int,int) still returns -1, signalling end of the compressed entry, regardless of the state of the underlying stream.
CSVFormat.EXCEL has allowMissingColumnNames set to true, i.e. calling EXCEL.getAllowMissingColumnNames() returns true (previously it returned false).
CSVFormat.MYSQL is configured with the null string equal to the literal two-character text "\N" (backslash followed by N): getNullString() returns "\\N" and isNullStringSet() returns true.

CSVRecord.putIn (and hence CSVRecord.toMap, which delegates to putIn) no longer throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException / fails when a mapped column's index is not less than the record's value count (values.length); such an out-of-range column is simply skipped, so the produced map contains no entry for that header. Mapped columns whose index is less than values.length are still populated with their header-to-value mapping.

TypeAdapters.NUMBER.read (used when deserializing to a Number-typed target, e.g. gson.fromJson("\"5\"", Number.class)) accepts a JSON STRING token and returns a Number representing that string's numeric value, instead of throwing a JsonSyntaxException — i.e. a quoted numeric string literal deserializes to a Number in the same way an unquoted NUMBER literal does.

For a Map type whose raw class is assignable to java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentMap but NOT to java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentNavigableMap (e.g., the ConcurrentMap interface), the ObjectConstructor's construct() returns a java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap instance.

When UnsafeAllocator.newInstance is invoked (via any of the reflection-based allocation strategies) with a Class argument that is an interface, it throws java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException (with message "Interface can't be instantiated! Interface name: <interface name>") instead of attempting to allocate an instance.

NumberInput.parseBigDecimal(String) with a non-empty String that new BigDecimal cannot represent (e.g. "NaN") does not throw the JDK's raw NumberFormatException from the constructor; instead it throws a NumberFormatException whose message is "Value \"<the input string>\" can not be represented as BigDecimal". Input that new BigDecimal can parse must still return the equivalent BigDecimal value.

During AnyGetterWriter.resolve, if the installed any-getter serializer implements ContextualSerializer it is subjected to primary property contextualization (SerializersProvider.handlePrimaryContextualization) bound to the any-getter's bean property, and the output of that contextualization becomes the effective serializer used for the any-getter.

Serializing a BigDecimal value whose property/type declares STRING format shape while JsonGenerator.Feature.WRITE_BIGDECIMAL_AS_PLAIN is ENABLED and whose scale is outside [-9999, 9999] (|scale| > 9999) fails with a JsonMappingException (via provider.reportMappingProblem) whose message names the offending scale and the [-9999, 9999] bound, rather than writing any output.
Calling writeObject(null) on a TokenBuffer writes a JSON null value (i.e. a VALUE_NULL token) rather than storing null as a VALUE_EMBEDDED_OBJECT embedded token.

A BeanPropertyWriter instance can be round-tripped through standard JDK serialization (java.io.ObjectOutputStream/java.io.ObjectInputStream) without throwing (NotSerializableException or otherwise): the class now implements java.io.Serializable.

In ExternalTypeHandler._deserialize, when the buffered token stream for the external-type property begins with a JSON null value (JsonToken.VALUE_NULL), the method returns Java null immediately instead of merging the type-id and value into a wrapper array and invoking the property deserializer.

A TokenBuffer created via TokenBuffer(JsonParser, DeserializationContext) has BigDecimal forcing for buffered floats enabled exactly when the supplied DeserializationContext is non-null and has DeserializationFeature.USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS enabled; if the context is null or the feature is disabled, forcing is off.

JacksonAnnotationIntrospector.findNameForSerialization(Annotated), for a member that carries no @JsonGetter and no (explicit) @JsonProperty, treats a member annotated with @JsonBackReference, @JsonManagedReference, or @JsonUnwrapped as implying an implicitly-named serialization property: it returns PropertyName.construct("") rather than null (so that the member is still discovered as a serializable property whose name is resolved by default), just as members annotated with @JsonSerialize, @JsonView, or @JsonRawValue already are.

For the deprecated CollectionType.construct(Class<?> rawType, JavaType elemT): when rawType declares exactly one generic type parameter, the returned CollectionType exposes a single content binding mapping that parameter to elemT — observable via containedTypeCount()==1 with containedType(0)/containedTypeName(0) referring to the elemT type binding — whereas when rawType declares zero type parameters or any other count, the returned CollectionType exposes the empty type-binding set (containedTypeCount()==0).

TypeFactory.constructType(Type, JavaType contextType) returns the JavaType for the given type rather than throwing when contextType is null, resolving it with no binding context — i.e. the same result as constructType(type) (empty bindings).

In deserializeSetAndReturn (reachable via deserializeAndSet), when the parser's current token for the object-id-source property is a JSON null (JsonToken.VALUE_NULL), the method returns null immediately without invoking the value deserializer and without performing any readable-object-id lookup or item binding, and without decorating/binding the currently-being-deserialized instance.

When MapperFeature.AUTO_DETECT_GETTERS is disabled, DeserializationConfig.getDefaultVisibilityChecker() returns a VisibilityChecker whose getter visibility is set to Visibility.NONE (so getters are not auto-detected as properties during deserialization introspection).

In TypeDeserializerBase._findDeserializer, when a type id is resolved by the type id resolver (typeFromId) to a JavaType that itself already carries generic type parameters (hasGenericTypes() is true), that resolved type is kept as-is: its generic type parameters are NOT re-derived by narrowing against the base type's raw class via constructSpecializedType(_baseType, rawClass). Only when the resolved type is non-generic (has no generic type parameters) does the pre-existing narrowing to constructSpecializedType still occur.

For a bean property with inclusion ALWAYS/NON_NULL/default where SerializationFeature.WRITE_EMPTY_JSON_ARRAYS is disabled, empty values are suppressed (via BeanPropertyWriter.MARKER_FOR_EMPTY) when the property's effective serialization type — the type after refinement by @JsonSerialize(as=...) annotation override or static typing — is a container type, even if the property's declared field type is not itself a container type.

JavaType.withHandlersFrom(JavaType src) returns a JavaType that carries the same own-level type handler and value handler as `src` when those differ from this type's own handlers: the returned type's getTypeHandler() equals src.getTypeHandler() and getValueHandler() equals src.getValueHandler().

For an ISO-8601 date-time with no explicit timezone indicator (reaching the branch that appends 'Z'), StdDateFormat pads the trailing time portion up to a full 12-character 'HH:mm:ss.SSS' so fully-normalized forms parse to the correct GMT instant: when less than three fractional-second digits follow full seconds, zeros are appended to reach three digits, and when the whole sub-millisecond/fraction tail is absent the literal '.000' is appended once before the 'Z'.

When a delegating key deserializer (DelegatingKD) deserializes a Map key, the wrapped delegate JsonDeserializer reads its input from a dedicated parser whose token stream contains exactly that key's text (written as a string value), instead of from the underlying document parser that was in the middle of reading the surrounding JSON.

CreatorCollector.addPropertyCreator records the supplied property list as the property-based creator arguments only when the offered property-based creator is actually adopted for the property-based slot (i.e. it replaces/becomes the stored C_PROPS creator). If the offered property-based creator is rejected by verifyNonDup in favor of an already-registered property-based creator, the previously recorded property-based arguments are left unchanged rather than being overwritten by the rejected candidate's properties.

When EnumSerializer.createContextual computes the property-level serialization decision for an enum object whose property carries a @JsonFormat whose shape does not positively dictate a form (shape absent/unspecified, or Shape.ANY, or Shape.SCALAR), that undetermined shape no longer overrides the serializer's pre-existing static choice: the surviving serializer keeps the prior _serializeAsIndex decision instead of reverting the property to dynamic resolution based on SerializationFeature.WRITE_ENUMS_USING_INDEX.

collectAndResolveSubtypesByClass(MapperConfig, AnnotatedMember property, JavaType baseType) with a null `property` (and non-null baseType) does not fail: it skips collection of subtypes from the property's own declared subtype annotations and still produces the result based on registered types and base-type-hierarchy annotation-derived subtypes. (When a non-null baseType supplies the raw base class, a null property no longer triggers a NullPointerException at the property-subtypes step.)

Calling getSuperClass() on a ResolvedRecursiveType whose referenced type has been resolved (via setReference) returns the result of _referencedType.getSuperClass() (i.e. the super class as seen through the resolved self-referential type's hierarchy), rather than the null/superClass field the placeholder itself carries.

The date-format list exposed in the ParseException message thrown when parsing fails (built from ALL_FORMATS) now includes the additional timezone-less ISO-8601 format string 'yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'.

DeserializerCache treats a map-like type whose key type carries a custom value handler as having custom handlers even when the type's content type has no value handler and no type handler; concretely this excludes such a map type from the cached-deserializer store — a cached-entry lookup for it returns null (forcing deserializer reconstruction) and a freshly constructed deserializer for it is not added to the cached-deserializer map, so repeated resolution of such a map type does not reuse a prior installed deserializer.

For an element whose content after its (possibly empty) attribute list consists of non-whitespace character/CDATA text immediately followed by a nested START_ELEMENT (true mixed content), XmlTokenStream returns the collected text as an XML_TEXT token — with that text exposed via getText() — rather than discarding the text and jumping straight to the nested element.

When parsing the portion following any combinator (`>`, ` `, `+`, `~`, `,`), an attribute-selector group written in balanced brackets [...] is consumed as a single atomic unit, so separator characters that are themselves combinator tokens (spaces, `>`, `~`, `+`, `,`) occurring inside the brackets (e.g. in the attribute value) do not terminate/split that sub-query; the whole bracketed expression remains part of the sub-query.

org.jsoup.parser.Parser exposes a new public static method parseBodyFragmentRelaxed(String bodyHtml, String baseUri) that parses bodyHtml as HTML into the body of a Document shell (as a body fragment) and returns the parsed Document.

Cleaning a source body whose element content is nested deeply (deep enough that the previous recursive cleaner overflowed the call stack) no longer throws StackOverflowError: Cleaner.clean(Document) and Cleaner.isValid(Document) complete on such deeply nested content instead of crashing.

Element.clone() returns a clone whose lazily-derived class-name set is its own independent copy (derived from the clone's own copied class attribute), not a set shared/aliased with the source element; consequently, adding, removing, or toggling a class on the clone (via addClass/removeClass/toggleClass/classNames(Set)) does not change the set of classes the source element reports through classNames()/hasClass(String), and a class-list mutation on the source does not alter the clone's reported classes.
When a start tag contains unrecognized input that yields an empty attribute key AND an empty attribute value (e.g. stray punctuation such as '

When the byte stream passed to DataUtil.parseByteData begins with a UTF-32 byte-order-mark (big-endian bytes 00 00 FE FF, or little-endian bytes FF FE 00 00), the content is decoded using the UTF-32 charset, this BOM override taking precedence over any explicitly supplied charsetName or any meta-tag-detected charset, so the parsing is performed on correctly decoded text.

TokenQueue.chompBalanced opens/closes its quote-tracking region only on un-escaped quote characters: a single- or double-quote character immediately preceded by a backslash (the escape char) does not toggle into or out of the quoted region, consistent with the existing backslash-escape handling for the balanced opener/closer characters.

A self-closing start tag for an unknown/custom element (e.g. '<foo/>') does not produce the "Tag cannot be self closing" parse error, and the element is retained as self-closing so that it round-trips in serialized output with the trailing slash ('<foo/>').

After Document.normalise() runs on a document that contains more than one head element, all head elements except the first one in document order are removed and their child nodes are moved into that first, surviving head element, leaving exactly one head.

A LeafNode (e.g. a TextNode or other leaf) now behaves as a node with zero child nodes for every Node operation that queries or traverses child nodes: child-enumeration operations that previously raised UnsupportedOperationException ('Leaf Nodes do not have child nodes.') from ensureChildNodes() now return/act on an empty child-node list instead — concretely childNodes() and childNodesCopy() return an empty list, childNode(index) accesses an empty list, and unwrap()/childNodesAsArray() treat the leaf as having no children rather than throwing.

When DataUtil.parseInputStream is given a null charset, finds no BOM and no <meta> charset, and the first child node of the resulting first-pass UTF-8-parsed document is a Comment whose data constitutes an XML declaration (i.e. it passes Comment.isXmlDeclaration) that names 'xml' and carries an 'encoding' attribute — the situation arising when the HTML parser tokenizes a leading <?xml version="..." encoding="X"?> prolog as a Comment rather than directly as an XmlDeclaration — the foundCharset is set from that declaration's encoding attribute, so the full stream is re-decoded using charset X (mirroring the behavior already present when that first child is a genuine XmlDeclaration). Observable upshot: e.g. Jsoup.parse(stream of bytes in iso-8859-1 beginning with <?xml version="1.0" encoding="iso-8859-1"?>, null, uri) yields a Document whose text content is decoded with iso-8859-1 rather than the default charset.

Comment.asXmlDeclaration() constructs an XmlDeclaration only when re-parsing the comment data (with data's first and last characters stripped and wrapped as '<...>') using the XML parser yields a Document that has at least one child ELEMENT (as reported by Element.children()); when the re-parsed Document has no element child (i.e. contains only non-element child nodes such as text/comment/data nodes, or is empty), asXmlDeclaration() returns null and the comment is left as a plain Comment (rendered as <!--data-->) rather than being turned into a mis-formed XML declaration.

Attribute.getValue() returns an empty string ("") rather than null when the attribute's stored value is null (as for a boolean attribute such as "hidden" parsed from HTML). Non-null values are returned unchanged.

Adding a header (via header/addHeader, which routes values through fixHeaderEncoding/looksLikeUtf8) whose ISO-8859-1 byte form ends with an incomplete UTF-8 multi-byte sequence whose continuation range reaches or exceeds the end of the data no longer throws an out-of-bounds exception; instead the value is accepted and stored unchanged (i.e., not treated as valid-looking UTF-8 and therefore not re-decoded to UTF-8).

FormElement.formData() excludes a form control element from the returned key/value data when the element's type attribute is "button" (case-insensitively, e.g. "BUTTON"), even if that element is otherwise form-submittable, enabled, and named.

DOMNodePointer.testNode for an element node: when matched by a NodeNameTest whose local name equals the element's local name (or whose name test is wildcard with non-null prefix), and the element's resolved namespace URI is null (the DOM node has no resolvable in-document namespace binding, e.g. a namespace-unaware document), the element is additionally treated as matching that name test if the name test's prefix equals the element's literal prefix — even when comparing the test's namespace URI against the node's null namespace would not have matched.

PropertyPointer.getLength() returns 1 (instead of the 0 previously produced via ValueUtils.getLength(null)) when the underlying property value, getBaseValue(), is null, so that a property whose raw value is null is treated as spanning a single node rather than as an empty span.

When a comparison operand is a Pointer, the comparison always proceeds on that pointer's dereferenced value (getValue()); the prior fast path that treated two Pointers as equal (returning true) before inspecting their values is removed, so a two-pointer comparison is decided by comparing their dereferenced values via the standard type-based equality/inequality rules.

indexOfAny(CharSequence, char[]) does not report a hit at the position of a cs character that is only a code-unit match: when cs's char at i is a high surrogate at a non-terminal cs position whose matching char in searchChars is a high surrogate at a non-terminal search position, indexOfAny returns i (the high surrogate's index) only if the immediately following code unit in cs equals the immediately following code unit in searchChars (i.e. the same supplementary character); otherwise it continues searching past i.

After DSCompiler.atan2(y, yOffset, x, xOffset, result, resultOffset) returns, the 0th-order (value) element result[resultOffset] is set to FastMath.atan2(y[yOffset], x[xOffset]) for every input, thereby yielding the IEEE atan2 value in the special cases (+0/+0, +0/-0, -0/+0, -0/-0, and ±infinity combinations) where the branch-based derivative value computation produces an incorrect or NaN result.

guessParametersErrors throws an EstimationException for insufficient degrees of freedom (message reporting the parameter count) if and only if the number of measurements is less than or equal to the number of unbound parameters of the problem.

In AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer the square-root matrix of a DiagonalMatrix weight (as surfaced by getWeightSquareRoot()) is itself produced as a DiagonalMatrix whose (i,i) entry equals FastMath.sqrt of the corresponding input diagonal entry, computed directly along the diagonal rather than via EigenDecomposition; for a non-diagonal weight matrix the general (EigenDecomposition-based) square root continues to apply.

When bounds are active, encode() maps each objective coordinate x[i] to x[i]/(boundaries[1][i]-boundaries[0][i]) rather than to (x[i]-boundaries[0][i])/(boundaries[1][i]-boundaries[0][i]); i.e. the normalized value no longer carries the lower-bound offset (so it is not shifted toward 0 by subtraction of the lower bound magnitude).

When a user-supplied convergence checker reports convergence during an iteration, doOptimize returns the best point (per goal) among the initial guess and every trial point evaluated across all iterations up to and including the current one — i.e. the globally best point encountered, not merely the better of the last two consecutive points (current/previous).

When the computed least-squares quantities take the direct, otherwise well-conditioned solution branch (both amplitude/omega ratios non-negative) yet the denominator coefficient c2 is exactly zero, the automatic parameter-guess procedure now aborts by throwing MathIllegalStateException (ZERO_DENOMINATOR) instead of silently continuing to evaluate a = sqrt(c1/c2) and omega = sqrt(c2/c3), which would divide by zero and yield NaN/Infinity parameter values.

In computeGeometricalProperties, when getVertices() returns an empty loop array (v.length == 0), the region is reported as covering the whole space (getSize() = POSITIVE_INFINITY, barycenter = NaN) only if the underlying BSP tree has no cut (getTree(false).getCut() == null) and its root attribute is TRUE; in every other empty-loop case — including a degenerate/empty region whose BSP tree still has a cut node — getSize() is 0 and the barycenter is Vector2D(0,0).

In the solution point returned by SimplexTableau.getSolution(), an original decision variable whose tableau column is basic in the objective-function row (tableau row 0) is reported with value 0 — rather than being read from that row's RHS — regardless of the objective row's right-hand-side entry and regardless of the negative-variable ('x-') shift term used for unrestricted decision variables.

The OpenMapRealMatrix(int, int) constructor throws a NumberIsTooLargeException when the product of (long)rowDimension and (long)columnDimension is greater than or equal to Integer.MAX_VALUE, rather than constructing the matrix; dimension pairs whose product is strictly below Integer.MAX_VALUE are accepted and the matrix is built normally.

When a REGULA_FALSI-configured secant solver is run and, during an iteration in which the new approximation does not cross onto the opposite side of the root (f1*fx >= 0, so the interval is NOT inverted), the computed approximation x equals the current upper bound x1, the solver immediately throws a ConvergenceException instead of continuing to iterate until the maximum number of evaluations is exhausted.

The 4-argument optimize(f, goal, min, max) launches the multi-start run with an initial start value equal to the midpoint of the search interval (min + 0.5*(max - min)), not with the fixed constant 0, so that even search intervals that do not contain 0 begin their first attempt from a point inside [min,max].

equals(double, double) no longer requires exact `x == y`; for two finite, non-NaN doubles it now returns true whenever they are separated by at most one representable ulp (i.e. the same tolerance as equals(x, y, maxUlps=1)), rather than only when x equals y exactly.

When a non-null VectorialConvergenceChecker is configured, doOptimize evaluates checker.converged against the last accepted trial's pair only (inside the successful-iteration branch), and applies no convergence-checker return on rejected probes; the checker is therefore never consulted about a rejected candidate.

The stop condition evaluated when processing a firing event is the disjunction (OR) of stop() across all registered event states at that event time, not just the currently firing state: if any handler requests stopping when its state is advanced to the event time, isLastStep becomes true and the integration terminates at that event time.

MathUtils.distance(int[] p1, int[] p2) computes the L2 (Euclidean) distance using floating-point (double) accumulation of the per-coordinate squared differences, so that for any two int-coordinate arrays it returns an accurate, finite non-NaN result even when the coordinate differences are large enough that the intermediate sum of squared differences exceeds the range of a 32-bit signed int (i.e., the result is no longer corrupted by integer wraparound of the accumulator).

UnivariateRealSolverUtils.bracket(function, initial, lowerBound, upperBound, maximumIterations) treats an expanded interval [a,b] on which f(a)*f(b) == 0.0 (i.e. at least one endpoint value is exactly zero) as a successful bracketing and returns the two-element array {a, b}, instead of throwing ConvergenceException.

When the denominator degrees of freedom is strictly less than or equal to 2.0, FDistributionImpl.getInitialDomain returns 1.0 rather than the raw mean formula (which would yield a negative value when denom df < 2 and positive infinity when denom df == 2 because it divides by (d - 2.0)).

A deep-stub mock newly created as a method-call return value through ReturnsDeepStubs is Serializable (its creation settings include serializable()), so that mock object alone can be serialized and deserialized.
Primitives.primitiveValueOrNullFor(double.class) returns a value of the double wrapper type (Double) equal to 0.0, rather than an Integer-typed boxed 0 that would fail to be used as a double.

While mocks are being injected into a single @InjectMocks-annotated object (the per-@InjectMocks-instance candidate pool shared across that object's entire class-hierarchy walk), once a mock is successfully injected into one field of that object it is removed from the candidate pool, so the same mock instance is never injected into any other field of that same object — a single mock ends up in at most one of that object's fields.

When the Same matcher's wanted value is null, the token written into the description in the position of the wanted value (between the '(' and ')' in the 'same(...)' text) is the literal string "null".

When InvocationMatcher.captureArgumentsFrom processes a varargs invocation, the matchers occupying the vararg region are deduplicated by their underlying matcher — unwrapping MatcherDecorator instances (e.g. LocalizedMatcher) before identity/hash comparison — so that multiple matcher occurrences backed by the same actual matcher are collapsed to one; each such distinct matcher then captures the invocation's full vararg element set exactly once, never re-capturing the same elements for each repeated matcher occurrence.

Matchers.isA(clazz) reports its InstanceOf matcher and returns, as the stub/matcher result value, the default argument yielded by HandyReturnValues.returnFor(clazz): when clazz is a primitive-wrapper type such as Integer.class, isA returns a zero-valued instance of that wrapper (e.g. Integer 0) instead of null, so using isA(Integer.class) as an argument matcher for a method whose parameter is the auto-unboxed primitive type int does not throw an unboxing NullPointerException.

In comparing an argument against a matcher's string description (the toStringEquals path used for suspicious-argument detection), a null argument does not throw a NullPointerException: the null argument is treated as having the string representation "null", so a matcher whose StringDescription is the literal string "null" is considered to have an equal string representation.
UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo(DurationField) returns 0 for any argument, whether or not the argument field is supported (it no longer returns 1 when the argument is supported).

When ZoneInfoCompiler.verbose() is called on a thread that has never previously stored a value in the cVerbose thread-local (i.e. no prior ThreadLocal.set on that thread), it returns false instead of throwing a NullPointerException as a result of the underlying thread-local value being null.

DateTimeZone.getOffsetFromLocal, when its two initial offset estimates agree (offsetLocal == offsetAdjusted) and that offset is zero (rather than only when it is strictly positive), applies the same overlap/just-after-a-transition correction it applies for positive offsets: for a local moment lying within one offset-diff of the preceding transition (previousTransition(instantAdjusted) < instantAdjusted and instantAdjusted - prev <= offsetPrev - offsetLocal), it returns the earlier/pre-transition offset offsetPrev instead of unconditionally returning offsetAdjusted. In particular, an ambiguous local wall-time in a zone whose candidate post-transition/standard offset is UTC (offset 0) no longer resolves to the later (zero) offset but to the earlier offset that applied just before the cutover.

UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo(DurationField durationField) returns 1 when the passed durationField.isSupported() is true, and returns 0 when the passed durationField.isSupported() is false (it no longer returns 0 unconditionally).

When computeMillis is invoked with resetFields=true on a bucket holding two or more saved fields, the returned instant is computed so that, after the saved fields have been applied in priority (sorted) order with round-floor resetting, they are applied a second time with reset/round-floor applied only to the last (highest-priority/smallest) saved field; consequently any finer field detail that an intermediate applied field's round-floor in the first pass would otherwise have discarded above the last field is recovered, so the returned millis reflects all saved field values consistently. (With resetFields=false, or a single saved field, the re-pass leaves the result unchanged.)

DateTimeZone gains a new three-argument overload convertLocalToUTC(long instantLocal, boolean strict, long originalInstantUTC): it returns instantLocal - getOffset(originalInstantUTC) directly when the resulting UTC instant's own getOffset still equals getOffset(originalInstantUTC) (original zone offset remains valid), and otherwise it behaves exactly like the pre-existing convertLocalToUTC(instantLocal, strict) (with that method's DST-gap/overlap and strict/non-strict handling).

When building a formatter from an ordered printer/parser element list whose first element is a Separator that has already been finalized (i.e. whose after-printer and after-parser were already assigned by a prior build), PeriodFormatterBuilder does not re-wrap that Separator around the trailing sublist; it instead keeps the Separator's existing finished printer/parser content intact and composes the full list (the separator followed by the remaining content) as its printer and parser. Concretely, a PeriodFormatter procured by appending an already-finalized leading-separator formatter (such as ISOPeriodFormat.standard()) into a fresh builder via append(...) and then calling toFormatter keeps all of that wrapped content, so that parsePeriod still recognizes the separator and the following fields instead of dropping them or throwing.
MutableDateTime.addWeekyears(0) leaves the instant (getMillis) unchanged, i.e. adding zero weekyears is an observable no-op.

When the target PeriodType supports months but not years (e.g. PeriodType.months()), normalizedStandard folds the entire combined year+month amount (including whatever years the period holds) into the months field and returns that result without raising an exception. Examples: 1 year 15 months normalizes to 27 months; -2 years 15 months normalizes to -9 months.

GJChronology.getInstance(zone, gregorianCutover, minDaysInFirstWeek) throws IllegalArgumentException when a non-null gregorianCutover resolves (in the target time zone, interpreted on the Gregorian calendar) to a date whose proleptic year is <= 0 — i.e. a cutover on or before 0001-01-01, such as LocalDate(-2,6,30) — so that no GJ chronology can be created whose cutover falls at or before Gregorian year zero. (Calling with a null cutover, which selects the default 1582 cutover, is unaffected.)

The AnsibleError raised for an installed collection directory lacking MANIFEST.json has a message that includes the collection name and states that a MANIFEST.json is expected if the collection has been built and installed via ansible-galaxy.
PamdService.remove removes a matched line that has both a previous and a following line by re-linking prev.next to next and next.prev to prev, incrementing the change count.

When state is present and want['text'] differs from have's text, map_obj_to_commands builds the banner command using want['text'] with leading/trailing newline characters removed but all other surrounding whitespace (spaces, tabs) preserved.

Changing the vrf to a non-default value on an unconfigured device yields commands ['management api http-commands', 'no shutdown', 'vrf <vrf>', 'no shutdown'] (state command appears both before and after the vrf command).

The ppc64 corpus scenario (ppc64-power7-rhel7-8cpu-cpuinfo) has expected get_cpu_facts result processor_count == 8 and processor_vcpus == 8, with processor_cores == 1 and processor_threads_per_core == 1.

LinuxHardware._replace_octal_escapes(value) returns the given string with every backslash-prefixed three-decimal-digit sequence (e.g. \040) replaced by the character whose value is that sequence interpreted in base 8 (\040 -> space), and leaves all other characters (including a backslash that is not followed by exactly three digits, and any shorter/longer digit run) unchanged.

GalaxyCLI.init_parser passes the description "Perform various Role and Collection related operations." to the superclass init_parser, so the ansible-galaxy CLI's top-level help/usage description mentions both Role and Collection operations.
is_special_comment(leaf) returns True if and only if the leaf's type is token.COMMENT or STANDALONE_COMMENT and its value starts with "# type:"; for any other leaf it returns False.
The black module no longer defines the exception classes FormatError, FormatOn, or FormatOff (attribute access black.FormatError / black.FormatOn / black.FormatOff raises AttributeError).

decode_bytes accepts empty input bytes (b"") without raising; when the byte stream contains no lines, it returns an empty decoded string together with the detected encoding and LF newline "\n" instead of raising IndexError.

EmptyLineTracker.maybe_empty_lines returns a `before` count of 0 for the first line it is asked about (i.e. when it has not yet processed any line, so `previous_line is None`), so no empty lines are emitted at the beginning of the formatted file even if the newline count of the first line's first leaf prefix (or any other part of the computation) would otherwise yield a positive count.

get_grammars(target_versions) with a non-empty target_versions set that contains at least one Python 2 version (e.g. {TargetVersion.PY27}) returns a list of exactly two grammars, in the order (python_grammar_no_print_statement, python_grammar) — i.e. the Python 3-style no-print-statement grammar is attempted first and the full Python 2 grammar second.

find_hook returns a list of absolute paths to ALL valid hook scripts matching the requested hook name (e.g. both pre_gen_project.py and pre_gen_project.sh are included when both exist), rather than only the first match.
cookiecutter.exceptions defines a FailedHookException class that subclasses CookiecutterException, so it can be imported and caught by name.
The path of a copied websocket route is the concatenation of the include_router prefix and the original route's path (prefix + route.path).
Constructing StackedRNNCells with `reverse_state_order=True` emits a deprecation warning (via warnings.warn) while still constructing the object successfully.

Conv2DTranspose.__init__ accepts a dilation_rate argument (default (1, 1)) and forwards it to the parent Conv2D/_Conv constructor so that the constructed layer's self.dilation_rate reflects the supplied value (normalized to a 2-tuple), instead of always being (1, 1).
Constructing a TimeseriesGenerator with a start_index+length that exceeds end_index (the effective start_index is greater than end_index) raises a ValueError; otherwise construction succeeds.

ctc_batch_cost preserves the per-sample (batch) dimension of label_length when squeezing: a label_length input of shape (samples, 1) yields a tensor of shape (samples,), including when samples == 1 (i.e. it does not collapse to a scalar when the batch dimension happens to have size 1).
ReduceLROnPlateau's constructor accepts a keyword argument named `min_delta` (default 1e-4) in place of the former `epsilon` argument, so `epsilon` is no longer a named parameter of the signature.

KerasRegressor.predict still forwards kwargs filtered through filter_sk_params(Sequential.predict) to self.model.predict, and its return value remains a numpy array (not a list) of the model's predictions.

SimpleTaskState.get_necessary_tasks excludes tasks in UNKNOWN status from the returned necessary set: an UNKNOWN-status task with scheduler_disable_time None contributes neither its own id nor its deps, exactly as DONE and DISABLED tasks are excluded.
The scheduler config exposes a boolean parameter `prune_on_get_work` (accessibly as an attribute of the scheduler Config object) that defaults to False.

SparkSubmitTask._dict_arg, when given a name and a non-empty dict, emits for each key/value entry the pair [name, 'prop=value'] with the formatted 'prop=value' text carrying no surrounding double quotes (previously the value was wrapped as '"prop=value"').

S3CopyToTable.run() binds its local load path to the value of the s3_load_path attribute itself (via attribute access that does not invoke it as a callable), rather than to the result of calling s3_load_path.

Parameter.parse_from_input accepts an optional third argument task_name (keyword-or-positional, defaulting to None) in addition to param_name and x, so callers may request a task-name-aware default resolution; calling it with only (param_name, x) remains valid.

In HiveCommandClient.table_exists with partition None, the containment check lowercases only the table argument and does not lowercase the stdout, so a stdout containing the table name only in uppercase characters still does not match a lowercase query name.

In the fallback (non-JSON) path, TupleParameter.parse returns tuple(literal_eval(x)), i.e. the ast.literal_eval result is coerced into a tuple, so any literal that evaluates to a non-tuple container (such as a bracketed list) is returned as a tuple rather than as that container type.

In Task.get_param_values, the ordered list of parameters that positional arguments are bound to consists of exactly the non-global parameters (params where is_global is False), in parameter-declaration order; global parameters are never bound from positional arguments regardless of their significant flag, and non-global parameters with significant=False are still positionally bindable.

_recursively_freeze converts a tuple value (and any tuple nested inside a Mapping or sequence) into a tuple of recursively-frozen elements, in the same way it already does for lists, rather than returning the tuple unchanged.
_partition_tasks records a set_tasks['ever_failed'] status containing every task that has a 'FAILED' entry in the worker's task history.

matplotlib.backend_bases._get_renderer no longer accepts the keyword-only parameter 'draw_disabled'; its signature is _get_renderer(figure, print_method=None), so passing draw_disabled raises TypeError.

nonsingular computes its interval/expansion logic on the endpoints' true numeric magnitudes rather than the input integer dtype, so that for integer inputs at the limits of their type (where abs() would wrap around, e.g. numpy int8 -128, or vmax - vmin would overflow) it returns the correct expanded float interval instead of a value derived from wrapped/overflowed intermediates.

matplotlib.transforms.nonsingular handles integer-typed (e.g. numpy integer) vmin/vmax endpoints correctly: it does not produce an incorrect result due to integer overflow or wraparound (such as `abs(np.int8(-128))` evaluating to -128, or `vmax - vmin` overflowing), and instead applies the normal singularity-expansion logic as if the endpoints were floats.
When the x-axis scale is not log (e.g. linear), non-positive limits passed to set_xlim are applied as given, with no substitution by the previous limits and no non-positive-limit warning.
Calling Axis.set_inverted on the base Axis class raises NotImplementedError (with message 'Derived must override') instead of modifying the view interval.
In Axes.scatter, an unfilled marker continues to force edgecolors to 'face' regardless of the linewidths supplied.

In init_ndarray, when the input values is not a 2D numpy ndarray (e.g. a 1-D ndarray or an existing ExtensionArray) and an extension-array dtype is in play, the resulting DataFrame has exactly one column containing those values.

Index.get_indexer_non_unique, when both the calling index and the target are all-dates (self.is_all_dates is True and target.is_all_dates is True), continues to derive the target values from target.asi8, so datetime-index-to-datetime-index lookups are unchanged.

DataFrame.append builds the row frame for an appended Series/dict using the index label Index([other.name], name=self.index.name) unconditionally, so the appended row's label is the Series name and the resulting frame's index name is self.index.name (rather than a default/unnamed index).

IntervalDtype is importable from pandas.core.dtypes.dtypes and is imported into pandas.core.dtypes.cast so that infer_dtype_from_scalar can construct interval dtypes (Interval inference is attempted only after the period check, so a value that is both is not treated as interval).
Categorical.min on an empty (zero-length) ordered Categorical returns the dtype's NA value (NaN) instead of raising an error or returning a category.

A float scalar .loc key on a CategoricalIndex whose categories are string/unicode/mixed is not rejected with a TypeError at the scalar-conversion step; the float key is passed through and the subsequent lookup of an absent label raises KeyError.

For the non-scipy interpolation path of missing.interpolate_1d (method in {'linear', 'time', 'index', 'values'}), when the x-axis / index values are not monotonically increasing, the interpolated result is nonetheless the value defined by the valid (x, y) pairs treated as a sorted set of knots, rather than the (incorrect) result of passing the unsorted x-knots directly to np.interp. I.e. the each interpolated point equals the linear interpolation between the two valid x-knots that bracket it in sorted order, using the y-value belonging to each of those x-knots.

pandas.melt() does not raise a KeyError for value_vars labels that are present in the DataFrame when the value_vars labels and the frame's column labels have mixed types (e.g. an integer column name listed alongside string column names); the presence check compares labels without coercing them to a common (string) dtype.

When a rejected dtype is passed, the raised exception is a ValueError whose message has the form "Incorrect `dtype` passed: expected <expected>, received <dtype>", where <expected> is 'signed integer' for Int64Index, 'unsigned integer' for UInt64Index, and 'float' for Float64Index.
Categorical.replace(to_replace, value, inplace=False) returns a new Categorical with the replacement applied when inplace is False, and returns None (mutating self in place) when inplace is True.
pandas.core.dtypes.missing._isna_ndarraylike accepts a keyword argument `old` (bool) that defaults to False, so existing callers can invoke it without the argument and get the non-inf-as-NA behavior.

NDFrame.interpolate raises ValueError (the 'No axis named ... for object type ...' error from _get_axis_number) when axis is not a valid axis for the object — e.g. axis=None, axis=2, or an unknown label — instead of failing with a Python unbound-local/NameError.

BaseGrouper.agg_series, when the fast aggregation path `_aggregate_series_fast(obj, func)` raises a TypeError whose message string contains the substring "ndarray", does not propagate that TypeError; instead it falls back to and returns the result of `self._aggregate_series_pure_python(obj, func)`.

should_series_dispatch returns True when one of the two operands' first-column dtype is datetime64 and the other's first-column dtype is object, regardless of which operand holds the datetime64 dtype and which holds the object dtype (previously only the left-operand-datetime64 / right-operand-object ordering returned True).

PandasArray.__setitem__(key, value) writes the value into the existing backing ndarray without changing the array's dtype: after any successful assignment self.dtype (and self._dtype) equals the dtype it had before the assignment; no upcasting to a wider result dtype occurs.

Block.to_native_types, in the branch where `self.is_object` is False and `quoting` is falsy, converts the (sliced) values into a fixed-width numpy unicode array whose itemsize is determined by the length of `na_rep` (i.e. `values.astype("<U{size}".format(size=writers.word_len(na_rep)))`) instead of `values.astype(str)`; the resulting array's dtype is therefore `<U` + len(na_rep) rather than `<U` + width of the longest stringified value.

The freq assigned to an addition/subtraction result is determined from both the operand (`other`) and the actual result object produced by the underlying operation; `_get_addsub_freq` is invoked with the computed result so its dtype can be inspected.

For an operand that exposes a scalar `dtype` attribute (a numpy ndarray or a 1-D Series), _can_use_numexpr includes that operand's dtype name in the set of dtypes considered for the numexpr dtype-compatibility check, so that such an operand's dtype can cause the check to return False when the dtype is not in _ALLOWED_DTYPES[dtype_check].

_normalize raises ValueError with the message "<margins_name> not in pivoted DataFrame" when margins is True and the given margins label is neither a component of the last row's index name nor equal to the last column's label (i.e. the margins label is not positioned as the final row/column of the table).
Index instances expose a `_supports_partial_string_indexing` attribute that is False by default on the base Index class.

For a PeriodArray, _validate_insert_value's compatibility check raises IncompatibleFrequency (DIFFERENT_FREQ message) when the inserted Period's freq does not match the array's freq, rather than silently re-casting the Period to the array's freq.

Calling a rolling aggregation named 'skew' with a BaseIndexer subclass as the window (e.g. df.rolling(<BaseIndexer>).skew()) no longer raises NotImplementedError; 'skew' is treated as supported so the computation proceeds and returns a result.

For a 1-dimensional object (ndim == 1), setting via `.at` with a tuple key of length greater than 1 assigns the value at that tuple label rather than raising: `series.at[1, 2] = 3` succeeds (and a subsequent `series.at[1, 2]` returns 3) for a Series with a single-level tuple-valued index, and `series.at[1, 3] = 5` succeeds for a Series with a two-level MultiIndex.

Because the Series derived from an Index `others` inherits the caller's index, the alignment/join branch of `cat` (guarded by `any(not data.index.equals(x.index) for x in others)`) is not entered for an Index `others` whose corresponding caller index matches, so no outer/left join is performed and the returned Series retains the caller's index.

IntervalArray.__setitem__ raises a ValueError with the message "Cannot set float NaN to integer-backed IntervalArray" when assigning a scalar NA value (e.g. np.nan, None) to an IntervalArray whose subtype is integer (int*/uint*), and leaves the array unmodified in that case.
The TypeError raised by Series.to_timestamp for an unsupported index carries the message "unsupported Type <name>", where <name> is the type name of the series' index.

When every date-unit attempt for the data raises (TypeError, ValueError or OverflowError), _try_convert_to_date returns the original unmodified data together with a failure indicator (False), so the caller treats the data as not date-convertible.

When XportReader is constructed with a file-like object (one that is neither str nor bytes, after the string-path handling in __init__), the reader adopts that object itself as its underlying buffer instead of reading its contents into a new in-memory buffer, so no copy is made and no encoding conversion is applied to the contents.

IntegerArray._values_for_argsort() does not raise (in particular not a ValueError from a minimum reduction on an empty selection) when the array has no missing values, including when the array is empty; it returns the copy of the underlying data unchanged.

PeriodIndex._engine resolves its values from the index's underlying PeriodArray (self._values) rather than from the PeriodIndex object itself, so that the engine's value getter yields a PeriodArray (which exposes .view('i8') and .freq) instead of a PeriodIndex.

_wrap_inplace_method's generated in-place operators (__iadd__, __isub__, __imul__, __itruediv__, __ifloordiv__, __imod__, __ipow__, __iand__, __ior__, __ixor__) clear the operand's parent-cacher link (the attribute set via _set_as_cached) as part of the operation, so that after `s op= other` on a Series that was obtained as a cached column of a DataFrame, the parent DataFrame is NOT updated with the new Series data (i.e. a column previously dropped from the frame does not reappear).

For a DataFrame-with-DataFrame flex arithmetic operation whose columns are not identical, when the operation is `**` (DataFrame.pow / DataFrame.__pow__) or the reversed `**` (DataFrame.rpow / DataFrame.__rpow__), the operation does NOT take the reindex-only-on-shared-columns path.
DatetimeIndexOpsMixin defines a `_is_comparable_dtype(dtype)` predicate that raises AbstractMethodError when called (it is abstract, to be overridden by the concrete datetime-like index subclasses).

DataFrame._get_value(..., takeable=True) obtains its column Series through DataFrame._ixs(col, axis=1), so the retrieved column Series is the frame's cached column Series for that positional column (it is marked as cached against `self`, and is named after the column label).
Categorical.from_codes raises ValueError with message 'codes cannot contain NA values' when `codes` is an integer-typed extension array containing any NA (missing) value.
Block.setitem raises a ValueError when the passed indexer is an np.ndarray whose ndim exceeds the block's own ndim, instead of proceeding to attempt the assignment.

When shift pads with the explicit Interval fill_value, only min(abs(periods), len(self)) pad entries are produced, so if abs(periods) exceeds len(self) the result length still equals len(self) and all entries equal fill_value.

The exact-shape-match condition in Block.setitem continues to be: the right-hand-side array is at least 1-dimensional, its first dimension equals the (transposed) block values' first dimension, and its total size equals the block values' total size (unchanged predicate, now hoisted into a variable reused by both the categorical branch and the pre-existing astype branch).

PeriodIndex.get_loc with a string key whose parsed resolution is finer than the index's freq does not raise when a non-None method is supplied; it uses the parsed datetime as the key and resolves through the period containing it (subject to method/tolerance).

The unstacked result of unstacking on a tuple-valued level name keeps the tuple names intact as level names: the levels that were not unstacked appear as the result's index name(s) and the unstacked tuple name appears as the name of the new column level (e.g., unstacking ("A", "a") from names [("A", "a"), ("B", "b")] yields an index named ("B", "b") and columns with a level named ("A", "a")).

Categorical.__contains__ returns self.isna().any() (i.e. True iff the Categorical contains at least one missing value) when key is a scalar NA value that is valid for the Categorical's categories dtype, as determined by is_valid_nat_for_dtype(key, self.categories.dtype); for example `np.nan in cat` is True exactly when the Categorical has any NaN value.

When a CustomBusinessHour offset is applied to a datetime (via BusinessHourMixin.apply) and the whole-business-day part bd is nonzero, the business days are skipped using the offset's own custom calendar (its weekmask, holidays, and calendar), so that dates falling on holidays or non-weekmask days are excluded from the day-skipping step; consequently the applied result advances only over valid custom business days when jumping whole business days.
response_status_message(status) returns a string of the form '<status> Unknown Status' when the status code has no entry in the HTTP reason-phrase mapping, instead of raising an exception.

The Content-Disposition header value is decoded as latin-1 with undecodable/invalid bytes replaced, so arbitrary byte sequences (e.g. b'.doc' with high-bit bytes) map to a Response class instead of propagating a UnicodeDecodeError; non-ASCII bytes in the filename are decoded via latin-1 rather than failing or being silently dropped.
WrappedRequest exposes a read-only attribute-style property 'host' that returns the netloc of the wrapped request's URL (same value as get_host()).
After a robots.txt download error for a netloc, RobotsTxtMiddleware leaves an entry for that netloc present in its parser cache (set to None) instead of deleting the cache entry.

A proxy CONNECT response delivered as a bytes object whose status line matches 'HTTP/1.x 200' is recognized by the response matcher, so the tunnel is established: the transport is switched to TLS and the endpoint's tunnel-ready deferred is called back with the protocol (instead of the match raising a str-pattern-on-bytes TypeError).
create_instance raises a TypeError when the constructor chosen (from_crawler, from_settings, or the class itself) returns None, instead of returning None to the caller.

ImagesPipeline.convert_image composites a palette-mode ('P') image over an opaque white background before converting it to RGB, rather than converting it directly to RGB, so that any transparency encoded in the palette is blended with white.

Class wiki_entity_linking.wikipedia_processor / method _process_wp_text: when no text body matching the `<text>...</text>` region can be found in the accumulated article text, the method returns (None, None).

The local filter_spans defined in examples/information_extraction/entity_relations.py, when two overlapping input spans have the same length, keeps the span that starts at the smaller (earlier) token index rather than the later-starting one.
The Errors class exposes an error code attribute named E175, whose value is the message template "Can't remove rule for unknown match pattern ID: {key}".

When get_new_command is called for a `man` command whose script contains neither '2' nor '3' and whose stderr does not indicate a missing manual entry, it returns a three-element list ordered as [man-3 variant, man-2 variant, last_arg + ' --help'], i.e. the last_arg --help suggestion comes last rather than first.

For a git/hub command whose stderr contains the substring "did not match any file(s) known to git.", the git_add rule's match() returns True even if stderr does NOT contain "Did you forget to 'git add'?" (the modern-Git stderr form without the add hint).

CorrectedCommand.run(old_cmd) logs the value of the PYTHONIOENCODING environment variable at debug level, using the literal placeholder `!!not-set!!` in place of the value when PYTHONIOENCODING is not present in the environment (when it is set, the actual value is logged).

sudo.match returns False for a command whose script starts with the token `sudo` (command.script_parts non-empty and command.script_parts[0] == 'sudo'), regardless of whether the command's stderr or stdout contains any of the permission-denied patterns that would otherwise cause a match.

Iterating, calling len() on, or indexing (with any index, including out-of-range) a SortedCorrectedCommandsSequence constructed over an empty iterable completes without raising an exception, and iterating/len() report an empty result (list(seq) == [], len(seq) == 0).

When the script contains no machine token (fewer than 3 space-separated tokens), get_new_command returns a single combined shell command joining 'vagrant up' with the original command, i.e. 'vagrant up && <original script>' without a trailing space before the separator.

Settings.update(**kwargs) returns a new settings object in which, for any key present in both the receiver and kwargs, the receiver's existing value is retained and the kwargs value is ignored; calling Settings({'key': 'val'}).update(key='new-val') yields a result whose 'key' attribute equals 'val'.
fix_file.match returns a falsy value when a pattern matches the stderr but the matched 'file' group does not name a path that exists as a file on the filesystem (os.path.isfile is false).

get_new_command produces its result by replacing the first occurrence of ' diff' in the script with ' diff --staged', so only the 'diff' token of the git subcommand (and any argument text) is preserved verbatim while the flag is placed after the diff token.
WebSocketProtocol declares set_nodelay(x) as an abstract method, so any concrete subclass of WebSocketProtocol that does not implement set_nodelay cannot be instantiated (TypeError).
RequestHandler exposes an overridable method `_break_cycles()` that, in its base implementation, sets self.ui to None; it can be called independently, not only from finish().

HTTP1Connection._can_keep_alive does not raise AttributeError when start_line is a response start line (i.e. an object without a `method` attribute), such as httputil.parse_response_start_line('HTTP/1.0 200 OK'); the call completes and returns a boolean instead of raising.

For a client-mode HTTP/1.1 request whose method is POST, PUT, or PATCH, which has no Content-Length header and whose Transfer-Encoding header is present with the exact value "chunked", HTTP1Connection.write_headers enables chunked output encoding (i.e. the body written is chunk-framed and finish() emits the terminating zero-length chunk) instead of treating the explicitly supplied Transfer-Encoding as an externally managed encoding.

AsyncHTTPClient.close() does not raise RuntimeError when the per-IOLoop instance-cache slot for self.io_loop holds the value None (e.g. when the entry was cleared by a weakref before a destructor-driven close runs); the call returns normally and leaves the client marked closed.

When a WebSocket client request is missing or has invalid required headers (Host, Sec-Websocket-Key, Sec-Websocket-Version), WebSocketProtocol13.accept_connection responds with HTTP status code 400 instead of aborting the connection.
tenumerate(iterable, start=N) returns an iterator whose yielded index values begin at N (matching builtin enumerate(iterable, start=N)) rather than always beginning at 0.

For a bare unary filter part `key` (no comparison operator) whose value in the dict is a boolean, _match_one returns True only when the value is True and returns False when the value is False — i.e. a boolean field with value False no longer passes the bare form even though it is not None.
dfxp2srt returns a unicode (compat_str) object containing the converted SRT data.
cli_bool_option still rejects a present parameter whose value is not a bool by raising AssertionError (the None case is the only value that bypasses the type check).

get_elements_by_class, get_element_by_class, get_element_by_attribute, and get_element_by_id inherit the valueless-attribute tolerance, since they all delegate to get_elements_by_attribute (e.g. get_element_by_class('foo', '<e attr class="foo">x</e>') returns 'x').

When the format-selector function produced by build_format_selector for a direct (single) format token is applied to an empty collection of formats, it yields no formats instead of raising an error (e.g. for 'best'/'worst' it no longer indexes into an empty list).

When ExtractorError is constructed with a truthy cause, the exception's message string includes the cause's repr, appended as ' (caused by <repr(cause)>)' after the message (and after any 'video_id: ' prefix), and this segment appears before the '; please report this issue ...' suffix when that suffix is added.
ArteTVPlus7IE._extract_from_json_url sets the resulting info_dict 'upload_date' from the JSON field 'shootingDate' when that field is present and non-empty, rather than from the 'VDA' field.

youtube_dl.utils exposes a function urlencode_postdata that URL-encodes its arguments (forwarding *args/**kargs to compat_urllib_parse.urlencode) and returns the result encoded as an ASCII bytes object rather than a str.
youtube_dl.utils exposes a module-level callable named struct_pack whose call signature is struct_pack(spec, *args) and which behaves like the standard struct.pack for all valid inputs.
url_basename returns u'' (rather than raising or returning None) for input URLs that do not match the pattern (no '//' host followed by a path).

When reading a table from a filename or file-like input with memmap=True, invalid-value masking (NaNs in float/complex columns and empty strings in character columns) is unconditionally disabled: mask_invalid is set to False regardless of the caller-supplied value of the mask_invalid argument.

Constructing a Time with format='byear' from a value that is a genuine quantity (exposes a 'to' method and a non-None 'unit') still raises ValueError with the message 'Cannot use Quantities for \'byear\' format...', but a value that happens to expose 'to' and 'unit' attributes whose unit is None is no longer rejected and is instead handled as an ordinary numeric Besselian-year input.

When called with as_image_hdu=True, fits_ccddata_writer (reached via CCDData.write) writes the CCDData data into an ImageHDU extension while prepending an effectively data-free PrimaryHDU as element 0 of the written FITS file, so the file's first HDU is a PrimaryHDU and the data lives in the following ImageHDU; when as_image_hdu is False or omitted, the file is written as before with the data in the PrimaryHDU.

When a WCS is constructed from a header whose (default-key) CTYPE codes end in '-TAN' on exactly two axes and at least one of those '-TAN' axes carries a PV keyword with subscript j >= 5, those CTYPE codes are rewritten to end in '-TPV' in the resulting core WCS (so the WCS uses the TPV projection) and the SIP distortion is not loaded (the resulting WCS.sip is None), while a FITSFixedWarning with message 'Removed redundant SIP distortion parameters because SCAMP' PV distortions are also present' is emitted.

Latex's to_string no longer unconditionally appends r'\,' immediately after the formatted exponential scale of a non-unity-scale CompositeUnit; the r'\,' separator is emitted only when the composite actually has basis units following the scale (so a scaled CompositeUnit with no bases produces no dangling thin-space separator).

The datetime appended to applied `--list` lines is the applied migration record's `applied` timestamp converted via strftime with the exact format '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', yielding a wall-clock string like '2021-01-01 12:00:00'.

When a relation column is the table's primary key (a PK-FK column), inspectdb generates the field definition as a OneToOneField rather than a ForeignKey, preserving the explicit `primary_key=True` parameter and still including `models.DO_NOTHING` (e.g. `models.OneToOneField(InspectdbPeople, models.DO_NOTHING, primary_key=True)`).

When add_never_cache_headers is applied to a response whose existing Cache-Control already carries a 'public' directive, the resulting Cache-Control no longer contains 'public' (it is replaced by 'private', per patch_cache_control's mutual-exclusivity between public and private) — i.e. the response's cached-by-shared-caches status is removed.

For a command that declares subcommands via parser.add_subparsers(), when a required argument declared on the selected subcommand's parser (rather than on the top-level parser) is supplied through call_command's **options, call_command forwards that required argument into its argument-parsing simulation and the command executes successfully — it does not raise (e.g. a ValueError from reading option strings, or an argparse error/CommandError about a missing required argument) during option reconstruction.
