When ServerHandler.cleanup_headers() runs for a response and the server that served it is not a socketserver.ThreadingMixIn instance (i.e. a non-threaded HTTP server), the 'Connection' header is set to 'close' even if the response does include a 'Content-Length' header, so the request handler's connection is marked for closing (close_connection becomes True) and a subsequent request is not kept alive on that connection.

QuerySet.query is exposed as a lazily-evaluated attribute whose read returns the queryset's underlying SQL Query; if the queryset holds a pending deferred filter (captured from an earlier filter()/exclude() made while the queryset was set to defer its next filter), the first read of .query applies that pending filter in-place to the underlying query and clears it, so later .query reads and all downstream operations see it applied exactly once (never skipped, never duplicated).

The django.db.models.query_utils.InvalidQuery exception class is retained but deprecated: evaluating isinstance(obj, InvalidQuery) returns True when obj is an instance of django.core.exceptions.FieldDoesNotExist or FieldError (as well as for actual InvalidQuery instances), and every such isinstance evaluation emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning deprecation warning with a message indicating InvalidQuery is deprecated in favour of FieldDoesNotExist or FieldError.

When django.forms.models._get_foreign_key is called with no fk_name and the model has more than one ForeignKey to parent_model (i.e. the pathological over-disambiguation case), the ValueError it raises now has the full message: “'<model._meta.label>' has more than one ForeignKey to '<parent_model._meta.label>'. You must specify a 'fk_name' attribute.” — i.e. the message appends the guidance sentence "You must specify a 'fk_name' attribute." to the pre-existing prefix.

When resolving a 'pk' ordering lookup (the pk shortcut), if the model's pk is a relation field (e.g. the parent pointer under multi-table inheritance) pointing to a model that declares its own Meta.ordering, SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name treats the lookup as an order-by-the-pk-column clause rather than substituting the referenced model's Meta.ordering in its place.

When a custom user model's USERNAME_FIELD is listed in its REQUIRED_FIELDS, the resulting auth.E002 checks.Error carries a non-None 'hint' whose text names the actual USERNAME_FIELD value (formatted with single quotes around it) and advises removing that value from 'REQUIRED_FIELDS'.

Each of Django's built-in signal singletons -- django.contrib.auth.signals user_logged_in/user_login_failed/user_logged_out, django.core.signals request_started/request_finished/got_request_exception/setting_changed, django.db.backends.signals connection_created, django.db.models.signals class_prepared/pre_init/post_init/pre_save/post_save/pre_delete/post_delete/m2m_changed/pre_migrate/post_migrate, and django.utils.autoreload autoreload_started/file_changed -- is now constructed without the providing_args argument, so importing these modules (which executes those definitions) and using the resulting signals never emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning.
ModelState.clone() returns a ModelState whose .fields is again an order-preserving dict keyed by field name with the same name->field content.

When the template engine parses a template containing the built-in {% ifequal %}{% endifequal %} tag (invoking the registered ifequal tag function), it emits a Python deprecation warning of category RemovedInDjango40Warning (a PendingDeprecationWarning subclass) with a message stating that the {% ifequal %} template tag is deprecated in favor of {% if %}.

When SessionMiddleware.process_response takes the session-deletion branch (SESSION_COOKIE_NAME present in request cookies and session empty), the deletion cookie is now written with samesite=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, so the emptied session cookie carries the SameSite attribute from the SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE setting.

When an app module's default_app_config does not equal the auto-detected configuration and automatic detection found no configuration at all (app_config_name is None), the emitted RemovedInDjango41Warning message contains the text "However, Django's automatic detection did not find this configuration." rather than referencing a (None) picked configuration.

call_command, when a required option or a member of a required mutually exclusive group is supplied via **options and that option's argparse action is one that stores a constant without taking an argument (store_true/store_false/store_const via _StoreConstAction, count via _CountAction, or append_const via _AppendConstAction), must pass it into the simulated parser as the bare option flag (e.g. '--flag') rather than '--flag=<value>', so the command executes instead of failing with an argparse parsing error/CommandError over an invalid '--flag=<value>' token.

In BaseFormSet.management_form, when the formset is bound and the submitted ManagementForm is invalid, the raised ValidationError (code 'missing_management_form') carries a message that begins with 'ManagementForm data is missing or has been tampered with' followed by a suffix 'Missing fields: <names>', where <names> is the comma-and-space joined list of form.add_prefix(field_name) applied to each field that appears in form.errors.

When a positional (non-keyword) argument passed to call_command (an element of the *args sequence) is a list or tuple, each element of that collection is stringified with str() and treated as a separate token in the simulated argument parse, so that a collection supplied for an nargs-style positional resolves to its individual parsed values rather than one token holding the whole collection's str() representation.

URLPattern.check() reports a system-check Error with id 'urls.E009' when the pattern's callback is a class (not an instance) that subclasses django.views.View, whose message describes the pattern and advises passing {ViewName}.as_view() instead of the class itself.

The durability nesting check of Atomic is subject to the class-level private flag Atomic._ensure_durability (True by default) such that when a subclass (or instance class) sets _ensure_durability to False, entering a durable=True atomic block nested inside another atomic block no longer raises RuntimeError.

When dumpdata runs with --output on a path whose extension is '.zip' (always) or '.bz2'/'.lzma'/'.xz' while the corresponding compression module (bz2, lzma, lzma) is not importable, the fixture is instead written as plain text into a file at the output path with that extension stripped, and a RuntimeWarning is issued whose text names the unsupported extension (e.g. "Unsupported file extension (.zip)") and the actual file the fixture was saved to (the basename of that stripped path).

Field.check() performs a new system check (_check_db_comment) that, for a field with a non-empty db_comment referring to a database whose connection does not advertise supports_comments (and whose model does not require the 'supports_comments' DB feature), returns checks.Warning id 'fields.W163' stating the DB does not support comments on columns (db_comment).

When migration_plan triggers the replaced-migration recovery path described above, it recomputes the plan from scratch over the entire targets sequence (preserving the caller's clean_start) against the replacements-disabled graph, so the returned plan correctly covers all requested targets rather than being a partial continuation of the interrupted loop.

BaseForm.get_initial_for_field returns the resolved initial value (the value from self.initial with the field's initial as fallback, or the result of calling a callable value) with its microsecond attribute zeroed (replace(microsecond=0)) whenever that value is an instance of datetime.datetime or datetime.time AND field.widget.supports_microseconds is False.

ManyToManyField.check() (via the _check_ignored_options machinery, wired through ManyToManyField.check and model-level check) returns a django.core.checks.Warning with id 'fields.W345', message 'related_name has no effect on ManyToManyField with a symmetrical relationship, e.g. to "self".', and obj set to the field, whenever the field's remote_field.symmetrical is truthy and a truthy related_name was explicitly supplied to the constructor (self._related_name). Conversely, no such W345 warning is emitted when either no related_name was explicitly supplied or the relationship is not symmetrical.

Every concrete cache-operation entry point across the db, dummy, filebased, locmem, and memcached backends (add/get/set/touch/delete/delete_many/has_key/incr/get_many/set_many and DatabaseCache.get_many key mapping) continues to produce a made key and subject that made key to the backend's key-validity check before performing the operation — the same observable warning/error behavior on invalid keys, now routed through make_and_validate_key.

When RelatedField._check_clashes() emits the 'fields.E302' Error (a reverse accessor name installed on the related model clashes with an existing field name on that related model, and the relation is not hidden), the Error message text exactly matches `Reverse accessor '{<related-model object_name>}.{<the accessor name>}' for '{<app_label.Model.field the defining field>}' clashes with field name '{<app_label.Target.field the clashing field>}'.` — i.e. the message begins by naming the actual reverse accessor being installed, qualified by the related model's object name.

In interactive superuser creation, when a REQUIRED_FIELDS option is supplied a non-None value via the command line (rather than being prompted), that value is validated by passing it through field.clean(value, None); if field.clean raises a ValidationError, the command terminates with a CommandError whose message is the ValidationError messages joined by '; ', rather than silently using the raw unvalidated value for the user.

Calling path() or re_path() with a kwargs argument that is not None and not a dict raises a TypeError whose message indicates the kwargs argument must be a dict and names the actual type passed (e.g. '...but got str.') instead of proceeding to build the pattern/resolver.

remove_non_capturing_groups(pattern) returns the input URL-regex pattern with each top-level non-capturing group (?:...) removed entirely — its '(?:' opening marker, its balanced matching ')', and all text between them are dropped, while all other text outside such groups is preserved in place — and this holds regardless of where the non-capturing group is located in the pattern (at the start, interior, or end) and regardless of whether its content itself contains further nested groups (which are removed along with the enclosing group). E.g. '^(?:\w+)a' -> '^a'; '^a(?:\w+)/b(?:\w+)' -> '^a/b'; '^(?:\w+(?:\w+))a' -> '^a'; '(?P<a>\w+)/b/(?:\w+)c(?:\w+)' -> '(?P<a>\w+)/b/c'; a pattern with no non-capturing group is returned unchanged.

QuerySet.iterator() called on a QuerySet that currently has prefetch_related() lookups set, with chunk_size omitted (None, the new default), emits a DeprecationWarning whose message starts 'Using QuerySet.iterator() after prefetch_related() without specifying chunk_size is deprecated.', and does not raise an exception.

When get_normalized_value (reached by related filters such as exact and __in over a relation, e.g. MyModel.objects.filter(rel=unsaved_instance)) is passed a model instance whose pk attribute is None (an unsaved instance), Django raises a RemovedInDjango50Warning deprecation warning bearing the exact message "Passing unsaved model instances to related filters is deprecated.".

When the autodetector generates an AddField for a field on an app/model and the same-change computation also removes a field of that identical name from that model (so the field name must be dropped then re-created, e.g. a ForeignKey/concrete field being replaced by a plain ManyToManyField), the resulting set of migration operations orders the re-adding AddField strictly after the matching RemoveField of that field name — never before it — so a single combined migration can apply both without relying on incidental list order.

When BaseDatabaseWrapper.on_commit is invoked with robust=True while the connection is in autocommit with no atomic block in progress (so func runs immediately), an exception raised by func is caught and logged instead of being propagated out of the on_commit call, which returns normally; when robust=False (the default), an exception from func propagates out of that immediate on_commit call unchanged.

Invoking the length_is template filter now emits, on every call, a deprecation warning of category RemovedInDjango51Warning with the message 'The length_is template filter is deprecated in favor of the length template filter and the == operator within an {% if %} tag.' (the warning is issued unconditionally, before any length/int computation and independent of the value/arg or the returned result).

When validating a Decimal whose value is zero expressed with a non-negative exponent (significand tuple (0,) and exponent >= 0, e.g. Decimal('0E+1') or Decimal('0E+2')), DecimalValidator counts it as a single digit (1), not as len(digit_tuple) + exponent digits.

When transaction.mark_for_rollback_on_error's guarded body raises an exception while the target connection is inside an atomic block, the connection additionally records that same exception (in the connection's new rollback_exc slot) rather than only setting needs_rollback, so the raised exception instance becomes retrievable via connection.rollback_exc afterwards.

QuerySet.aupdate_or_create accepts an additional keyword parameter create_defaults and forwards it (together with defaults) to update_or_create, so its observable behavior matches update_or_create when awaited.

In the ModelAdmin system checks, a list_display item whose value (obtained via obj.model._meta.get_field(item) or via the fallback getattr(obj.model, item)) is a reverse one-to-many relation (a reverse foreign key, i.e. the field's .rel exists and field.rel.field.many_to_one is true) is rejected with a checks.Error carrying id 'admin.E109' whose message reads "The value of '<label>' must not be a many-to-many field or a reverse foreign key.".

When converting a grayscale string specification, matplotlib.colors.to_rgba (via _to_rgba_no_colorcycle) raises a ValueError if the string parses to a float value outside the inclusive range [0, 1], instead of returning an RGBA tuple whose R/G/B components lie outside that range. The raised error message identifies the offending input as an invalid string grayscale value and states that the value must be within the 0-1 range (e.g. the message contains "Invalid string grayscale value" and "Value must be within 0-1 range").

When removing such a shared Axes, the surviving sibling's minor formatter is left untouched if its owning axis treats it as a default (isDefault_minfmt True), i.e. a default minor formatter is preserved rather than re-set/cleared.
RcParams.copy() returns a new RcParams instance (not a plain built-in dict) that holds the same key→value pairs as the source RcParams.

copy.copy of a TaggedValue returns a new TaggedValue holding the same value and unit as the original (shallow copy, sharing the underlying value object), rather than falling back to deep/reduce-based copying.

In PS/EPS output, when a clip-path that has not been seen before is drawn, RendererPS defines a bound PostScript procedure whose name is 'c' followed by the clip path's zero-based sequence number formatted in decimal (so the clip procedures defined/used in the emitted .ps/.eps file are c0, c1, ..., c10, ... rather than c0,c1,...,ca,cb,... for counts >= 10), and that decimal name (not a hexadecimal rendering) is the value cached in _clip_paths and re-referenced whenever the same clip path recurs.

ContourSet.find_nearest_contour(x, y, indices=None, pixel=True) raises ValueError (carrying the message "Method does not support filled contours.") when invoked on a filled ContourSet (self.filled is True), regardless of the value of the indices argument.

When tripcolor is called with neither a positional C argument nor a 'facecolors' keyword (facecolors is None and no positional arg remains after the triangulation spec is consumed), it raises a TypeError (not ValueError) whose message is "tripcolor() missing 1 required positional argument: 'C'; or 1 required keyword-only argument: 'facecolors'".

After applying a value range, the RangeSlider's filled selection polygon self.poly is (re)positioned to span from the low endpoint to the high endpoint along the slider's value axis while covering only the mid-width band (0.25 to 0.75) across the perpendicular track direction: for orientation "vertical" the fill spans the vertical data range across the horizontal .25–.75 band, and for "horizontal" it spans the horizontal data range across the vertical .25–.75 band.

After pyplot.switch_backend() completes a switch to a concrete (named, non-auto-sentinel) backend, the current shell's REPL/pylab display hook is (re)installed: in an interactive matplotlib session -- including an IPython '--pylab' session where install_repl_displayhook registers pyplot._draw_all_if_interactive as the IPython post_execute handler -- figures are automatically re-drawn at the end of subsequent input commands (interactive auto-redraw is active). This holds whether the backend load is the session's first lazy load through _get_backend_mod or a later explicit backend switch reached through any other entry point; previously the hook was installed only inside _get_backend_mod's `if _backend_mod is None` first-lazy-load branch, so a backend switch performed once a backend was already loaded (e.g. via an explicit switch_backend / matplotlib.use call) left the auto-redraw display hook unregistered.

Reading `_cachedRenderer` on a `SubFigure` does not raise AttributeError (even when the SubFigure has not yet been drawn, in which case previously the attribute was undefined on the instance) and returns the `_cachedRenderer` value of the SubFigure's parent figure (`SubFigure._parent`).

matplotlib.style.use (and the style.context context manager, which delegates to use) accepts, as a style specification, a string of the dotted form "package.style_name" where "package" is an importable Python package; the rcParams defined in the file located inside that package at <package>/style_name.mplstyle are read and applied (only the parameters actually listed in that file). Dotted names spanning subpackages (e.g. "dotted.package.name" resolving within dotted/package/) are likewise supported.

Calling Axis.set_ticks with labels=None (labels not provided) while passing additional keyword arguments raises ValueError with the message 'labels argument cannot be None when kwargs are passed', rather than silently ignoring those kwargs.

Changing a LineCollection's alpha (set_alpha) while it has a gapcolor set re-applies the gap color converted with the updated alpha, so the value returned by get_gapcolor() thereafter reflects the new alpha.

Text._get_layout computes the layout (bounding box, per-line metrics/parts, and descent) from the wrapped text returned by _get_wrapped_text() rather than from the raw stored text, so that when wrap=True (and usetex is False) the extent/reservation it reports reflects the wrapped multi-line rendering instead of a single long line — for wrapping widths that actually trigger one or more breaks. This makes all consumers of _get_layout (the returned bbox/info used, e.g., by get_window_extent and the layout-time tightbbox/constrained-layout paths that call _get_layout before draw) report the same, wrapped shape that draw renders.

Calling Figure.tight_layout() must not cause the figure to be re-armed with a working automatic tight-layout engine through the rc parameter figure.autolayout: in particular, when rcParams['figure.autolayout'] is True, after fig.tight_layout() returns the figure does not hold a freshly-installed TightLayoutEngine, so subsequent draws do not keep re-running tight layout as a side effect of the tight_layout() cleanup.

The width of the marker-edge strokes on the PathCollection returned by Axes.scatter is drawn from one unified driver regardless of spelling: whether supplied via the explicit plural parameter `linewidths`, or via the singular collection-alias keyword `linewidth`, and combining both forms, the value is resolved through Collection keyword normalization so that the final edge-stroke width is deterministic and matches the collection's resolved linewidth semantics.

When a shared sibling Axes's limit is updated as part of propagating an emitted limit change, that update is applied non-recursively (the sibling _set_lim is invoked with emit=False) and the sibling's own '{name}lim_changed' event is then fired at most once per originating change, so the event does not cascade or get re-emitted again through the shared-axis group.

seaborn.external.version.Version parses a PEP-440 version string (with optional epoch, pre/post/dev/local segments); constructing it from an invalid version string raises InvalidVersion (a ValueError subclass), and its ordering comparisons follow PEP 440 normalization so that e.g. '3.0' and '3.0.0' compare equal and pre/post/dev/local orderings are respected.

When a ContinuousBase scale is set up with norming enabled (prop.normed True) and with norm endpoints needing unit conversion (values from the data min/max when norm is None, or from the explicit norm), converting those endpoints via axis.convert_units yields Python floats, so the resulting normalization constants a=forward(vmin) and b=forward(vmax)-forward(vmin) are float-scalar numerics. This ensures the scale's normalize step maps each data value's forward-transformed coordinate to a correct finite normalized value (the vmin value mapping to 0 and vmax to 1) rather than failing or producing invalid/non-numeric result types (such as numpy datetime/timedelta values) when the endpoints are date/time or otherwise non-float unit-converted values.

When set_index forms a MultiIndex (two or more source coordinates merged) onto a dimension d, every other variable of the object that was still dimensioned along one of the absorbed source-coordinate names (because that source coordinate had served as the variable's own dimension) has that dimension rewritten to the MultiIndex dimension d in the result; no retained variable keeps a dangling reference to a dimension name that has become a MultiIndex level.

When xarray.combine_by_coords is called with fill_value=None, each group of datasets (after being ordered from dimension coordinates) must create a complete hypercube; if datasets are missing such that the group does not form a complete hypercube, combine_by_coords raises a ValueError instead of returning a Dataset with missing/filled values.

"nanoseconds" is a recognized unit in TIME_UNITS, so netCDF timedelta variables whose attrs units == "nanoseconds" are decoded (CFTimedeltaCoder.decode takes the decode path and yields a numpy timedelta64[ns] array) instead of being returned undecoded.

ZarrBackendEntrypoint now provides a guess_can_open that returns True only when filename_or_obj is a string whose extension from os.path.splitext is exactly '.zarr'; if os.path.splitext(filename_or_obj) raises TypeError (e.g. non-string input), it returns False. Previously zarr had no guess_can_open override.

xr.polyval returns an output whose non-degree broadcast dimension ordering is anchored on the evaluation coordinate `coord`: the Horner accumulator is seeded from a full broadcast (all-zero DataArray) matching `coord`'s dimensions/coordinates, placed as the leading operand of the first addition with the highest-degree coefficient term `coeffs.isel(degree_dim=max_deg, drop=True)`, so that when the leading-coefficient term and `coord` disagree in dimension order the returned array's dimension ordering/index structure and (DataArray) name follow `coord` rather than the coefficient array.
When `--output <file>` is supplied and opening or writing the file raises an OSError, pylint prints the exception message to stderr and terminates with exit code 32.

In expand_modules, while resolving a target given by module name, only an ImportError is swallowed and recorded as a fatal error entry; a SyntaxError raised during that resolution is no longer caught, so it propagates out of expand_modules instead of being added to the reported errors.

The new 'glob_paths_csv' argument type transforms a comma-separated list of path entries by expanding user (~) and environment variables and then expanding glob patterns recursively on each entry, returning the concatenation of all matched paths in entry order so that an entry matching nothing contributes no path and an entry matching several paths contributes all of them (paths that name a literal existing file/dir still pass through).
pylint.interfaces exports a CONFIDENCE_MAP dict that maps each confidence level name from CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_NAMES to its corresponding Confidence entry in CONFIDENCE_LEVELS.

When a confcutdir C is configured, conftest discovery treats a directory D as within confcutdir scope (so an ancestor conftest can be collected for it) if and only if D is not one of C's own ancestor/parent directories; only a directory strictly above C (a proper ancestor of C) is out of scope. In particular the confcutdir's own directory, its descendants, and directories that are unrelated to it (neither ancestors nor descendants of C, such as a sibling subtree) are all within scope.

Calling pytest.raises(expected_exception) with a falsy expected_exception (e.g. the empty tuple ()) immediately raises ValueError, raised by the raises() call itself before any code block runs or a context manager is returned, rather than deferring a less clear failure to context-exit or validation.

fit(X, y=None) remains available and continues to return self, and its observable fitting behavior is unchanged even though the implementation now performs the estimation by delegating to fit_predict(X, y) internally.

When copy_Xy is False but the supplied Xy array is not writeable (e.g. read-only or memmap-backed), _gram_omp no longer raises an error from its in-place coefficient-swapping; it makes an internal copy of Xy and returns the same coefficients it would have produced if Xy were writeable.

When fit on training data where the requested n_quantiles exceeds the number of samples (n_samples), QuantileTransformer.fit issues a UserWarning reporting that n_quantiles is greater than the total number of samples and that n_quantiles is set to n_samples.

When GradientBoosting.fit is called with an explicit sample_weight and the init estimator's fit (as happens with an sklearn Pipeline) raises a ValueError whose message contains 'not enough values to unpack', a ValueError is raised whose message is 'The initial estimator <init.__class__.__name__> does not support sample weights.', chained from the original ValueError

When `stratify` is supplied as a 2-dimensional (e.g. multi-label) array, resample supports stratification by treating each distinct row of stratify as a separate class (each row mapped to a single joined-string identifier), so that the per-row class proportions are approximately preserved in the drawn sample rather than failing or stratifying per individual column cell.

AffinityPropagation.fit(X, y) with affinity='precomputed' and X a scipy sparse matrix raises an error during input validation (check_array with accept_sparse=False), rather than accepting the sparse matrix and storing it as affinity_matrix_.

When fitting an AdaBoost* estimator whose estimator is not set and whose base_estimator is set to None, a FutureWarning is emitted whose message states that 'base_estimator' was renamed to 'estimator' in version 1.2 and will be removed in 1.4 (i.e. an explicitly-provided None base_estimator is treated as a deprecated use of the base_estimator parameter).

export_text accepts class_names given as any array-like (list, numpy array, and other array-like containers) of target-class labels; previously only a list was accepted. The provided names are used to label leaf classes in the returned report.

The hardcoded-extlink-detector external link checker does not emit its 'could be replaced by an extlink' replacement-suggestion warning when the captured value (the portion of the URI matching the extlink base pattern's %s capture) contains a forward slash '/', even if the URI otherwise matches an extlink base pattern with a non-empty value.
`inherited_members_option(arg)` for a falsy argument that is not True/None (e.g. False or an empty string) returns the empty set, so no ancestor-name filtering is requested.

When partitioning a docstring line into a leading part and its colon-separated description, a text run starting with the literal token ``:meta `` followed by further colon-delimited content (of shape `:meta KEY: VALUE...`, i.e. a ``:meta ...: ...`` construct) is treated as a single atomic/protected unit, so none of the colons inside it is taken as the leading/description boundary; text such as a ``:meta``-style embedded annotation on a parsed line is not split in the middle and remains attributed to the preceding field rather than being shifted into the description.

In GoogleDocstring/NumpyDocstring._parse_methods_section, when the docstring was processed with options that contain the 'noindex' key (i.e. the enclosing auto directive carried :noindex:), each generated '.. method:: <name>' line is immediately followed by an indented ':noindex:' option line (inserted before the description content and trailing blank line), so the emitted method directive carries :noindex:.

When autodoc_typehints == 'description' and a py object's contentnode is being transformed, if the contentnode's parent desc_signature node lacks the required context attributes (a missing 'module' and/or 'fullname', raising KeyError on attribute access), sphinx.ext.autodoc.typehints.merge_typehints must not propagate the KeyError to abort the build; instead it must cleanly return without modifying the contentnode or injecting any type-hint fields.

autodoc exposes a new public class `ObjectMember`; constructing `ObjectMember(name, obj, skipped=False)` yields an instance that behaves/comparatively equals the 2-tuple `(name, obj)` and additionally exposes attributes `__name__` (== name), `object` (== obj), and `skipped` (default False, settable to True).

Documenter.process_doc guarantees that, under an active app (self.env.app truthy), every non-empty docstring chunk it processes ends with exactly one trailing blank line: after the 'autodoc-process-docstring' event handlers have run (seeing the chunk without this added blank), if the chunk is non-empty and its last line is not the empty string '', a '' line is appended to the end of the chunk before its lines are yielded, and no extra blank line is added when the chunk is empty or already ends with ''.
The man builder registers a confval named 'man_make_section_directory' whose default value is False.

When the napoleon_use_param config option is enabled, the content of a 'Receives'/'Receive' section is rendered as docutils field-list roles, producing a ':param NAME:' description and, where a type is present, a ':type NAME: <type>' line for each parameter; comma-separated co-declarations (e.g. 'x, y: int') are split into separate :param:/:type: groups.

Setting up the `sphinx.ext.autodoc` extension now also sets up the `sphinx.ext.autodoc.preserve_defaults` sub-extension, which registers on the Sphinx application a configuration option named `autodoc_preserve_defaults` whose default is `False`.

During cross-reference resolution, when a pending_xref node contains a pending_xref_condition child matching 'resolved' first, or otherwise matching '*', the content element (contnode) handed to domain xref resolvers and to the 'missing-reference' event is derived from that matched condition's child content (preferring 'resolved' over '*') rather than from the raw first child of the pending_xref node; if no such condition child is present, it is derived from node[0] as before.

LaTeX printing of a FormalPowerSeries (e.g. the object returned by fps(f)) renders the series' infinite Closed-form representation s.infinite — the Add of the independent terms plus an unevaluated \sum (sigma) over the general term ak.formula * xk.formula running from k=ak.start to infinity — instead of the truncated finite polynomial expansion returned by s.truncate(). Concretely, latex(fps(f)) now contains an infinite Sum over the coefficient/general term and no longer trails the truncated 6-term expansion with a \mathcal{O}(...) order term.

CCodePrinter now prints Relational expressions (Eq, Ne, Gt, Lt, Ge, Le) as an inline infix C comparison '<lhs_code> <rel_op> <rhs_code>' with the C operator token and surrounding spaces (for example 'x != 0', 'x == c') instead of falling back to StrPrinter's representation (which rendered == ' as 'Eq(...)' and '!=' as 'Ne(...)').

An Add that is a pure complex 'number' r + i*I with r, i rational and with D = sqrt(r^2 + i^2) rational (a Pythagorean triple) evaluates a Rational power whose denominator (q) is 2 (e.g. the square root) to the closed principal-branch algebraic form sqrt((D - r)/2)^p * ((D + r)/abs(i) + sign(i)*I)^p (with the p-th power of the inner binomial expanded), rather than remaining an unevaluated radical; e.g. sqrt(3 + 4*I) yields the exact reduced value.

Calling the module-level sympy.polys.polytools.degree on a non-Poly, non-numeric Expr that has more than one distinct free symbol raises type-errors.TypeError when no explicit symbolic generator is supplied (i.e. when the gen argument is numeric, including its default value 0), instead of returning the degree with respect to the canonically-chosen first generator.

The simplify() signature is changed so that the former fourth keyword parameter `fu` is removed and replaced by a new keyword `rational` (default False), i.e. the signature is simplify(expr, ratio=1.7, measure=count_ops, rational=False); consequently a call that passes an explicit `fu=...` keyword now raises TypeError and a call passing `rational=...` (True, False, or None) is accepted.
For an argument z known to be real, sinh(z).is_positive equals z.is_positive (True iff z is positive real); for non-real z it is not asserted.

The sinc class no longer subclasses TrigonometricFunction; sinc is instead a direct subclass of Function. Consequently a sinc(...) instance is not an instance of TrigonometricFunction (whereas previously sinc(x).__class__ was a TrigonometricFunction with sinc being a sinc instance), while it remains an ordinary Function/Expr.
rcode / RCodePrinter translates a factorial function expression into an R call 'factorial(...)' of its argument, rather than reporting it as not supported.

binomial(n, k) auto-evaluates to n when n - k equals 1 (i.e. k == n - 1) and n is known to be nonnegative or a non-integer; in particular, binomial(n, n - 1) now evaluates to n for a positive-integer symbol n instead of remaining unevaluated.

count_ops counts operations across both the keys and the values of dictionary input: a Python dict is sympified to a Dict and then processed via the Dict path summing count_ops of each key and each value, and a SymPy Dict input is likewise processed over its key/value items (rather than only over its keys via generic iteration).

In the dict returned by sympy.logic.boolalg._finger, the fifth element of each symbol's fingerprint tuple is a sorted tuple of integer triples (i, j, k), where i is the number of arguments of an And- or Or-function appearing among the top-level arguments in which that symbol occurs as a non-negated Symbol literal, j is the number of that function's arguments that are Not(literal), and k is the number of such functions (sharing the same (i, j)) in which the symbol so occurs; a symbol that never occurs as a non-negated Symbol literal inside any And/Or top-level argument (e.g. it only occurs as a bare top-level symbol, as in x&~y, or only inside Not(·)) receives an empty tuple ( ) as its fifth element.

In Mul.matches, when the pattern (self) and the expression are both non-commutative products, the commutative (scalar) factors are separated from the non-commutative factors and matched among themselves first; a side whose product has no scalar factors is treated during that step as if it had the scalar factor 1.

Range accepts symbolic start/stop/step arguments (an argument that contains a Symbol and is not known to be non-integer, or is infinite) instead of raising ValueError; e.g. Range(i, j, k) with pure symbols constructs successfully and its .start/.stop/.step expose the supplied symbolic values (no literal-integer requirement). Finite literal non-integer arguments (e.g. pi) are still rejected with the 'Finite arguments to Range must be integers' ValueError.

Expr equality (__eq__) against a Python native string returns False regardless of the string text (e.g. Symbol('x') == 'x' is False and Integer(1) == '1' is False), rather than sympify-parsing the string content and comparing against it (which could otherwise make Symbol('x') == 'x' evaluate to True).
S.Rationals.boundary equals S.Reals (the whole real line), rather than Rationals itself.

latex() accepts a new optional boolean keyword argument parenthesize_super, defaulting to True, and forwards it into the LatexPrinter configuration; the LatexPrinter's default settings likewise define parenthesize_super to True (so a printer constructed without that setting also behaves as True).

SciPyPrinter._print_airyai maps a SymPy airyai function to the string 'scipy.special.airy(<printed arg>)[0]', where <printed arg> is the printer's rendering of the function's single argument (index 0 of scipy.special.airy, corresponding to Ai).

collect(expr, syms, evaluate=False), when syms contains a nonsymbol (an expression that is neither a Symbol nor -Symbol nor contains a Wild), returns a dict in which each value (the collected coefficient/Add expression for a key) has had the internal Dummy placeholders substituted back to the original input symbols, i.e. the coefficient values are expressed in terms of the caller's original syms/expr symbols and contain no leaked temporary Dummy variables. (Keys were already mapped back before this change; now values are mapped back too.)

Rendering a SingularityFunction that itself carries an outer exponent (a powered SingularityFunction, i.e. one printed through the LaTeX Pow path that supplies an `exp`) does not raise an error and yields the wrapped LaTeX form `{\left({\langle SHIFT \rangle}^{POWER}\right)}^{EXP}`, where SHIFT is the rendered argument-difference (args[0]-args[1]), POWER is the rendered internal exponent (args[2]), and EXP is the rendered outer exponent.

Each value in the relations dict passed to the CoordSystem constructor must, per stored (source-system-name, target-system-name) key, carry both the source system's coordinate symbols and the target's transformed-coordinate expressions: canonicalization stores an entry as the 2-tuple (tuple-of-source-symbols, tuple-of-target-expressions). A Lambda value is converted using its signature and expr; any other value has element [0] taken as the source-symbols tuple and element [1] as the target-expressions tuple.

UnitSystem._collect_factor_and_dimension still returns, as the factor (first) component of a Function expression, the expression's .func applied to the collected scale factors of its arguments (this wrapping of factors is unchanged); only the dimension component is no longer wrapped in the function.

MathematicaParser._from_mathematica_to_tokens tokenizes a comment-cleaned code split with the tokenizer regex (tokenizer.findall) only when that split is a str and is all-ASCII; a str split containing any non-ASCII character (e.g. a Greek letter such as λ) is instead appended to the returned token list as a single opaque token equal to the whole split, so the non-ASCII characters are preserved rather than silently dropped by findall. (Equivalently, the two cases that previously took the tokenizer route — a plain ASCII split and a non-ASCII split — now differ: the latter is not fragmented.)

When SkyCoord.__getattr__ is invoked for an attribute that is not handled by its forwarding logic (not a matching frame alias/name, not a frame attribute, not present on the underlying _sky_coord_frame, and not a frame name transformable to), the object defers to normal attribute lookup (self.__getattribute__) so that the AttributeError ultimately raised is the standard one from Python's attribute machinery / the attribute's descriptor — with its own message — rather than replacing it with a SkyCoord-crafted generic attribute-error message; this applies equally whether the attribute is genuinely absent (yielding the standard "'...' object has no attribute '...'" error naming the object's actual class) or present via a subclass property/descriptor whose getter raises its own AttributeError (which now propagates unchanged instead of being swallowed).

Header.fromstring accepts a `bytes` first argument (in addition to `str`) and builds a Header whose parsed cards are equivalent to parsing the latin-1 decoding of those bytes; arbitrary byte values (including non-ASCII, which latin-1 always decodes) are accepted without raising a TypeError/UnicodeDecodeError, with bytes passed onward to Card.fromstring for card parsing.

parse_duration, when matching the standard 'HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]' format, accepts an optional single leading '-' sign placed immediately before the time portion (before the hours term, or before the first term when there is no hours term), and that sign, when present, negates the entire time portion as a whole rather than only its leading (hours) term — e.g. "-01:02:03" yields a timedelta equal to negative (1 hour, 2 minutes, 3 seconds).

For an InlineModelAdmin on an auto-created M2M implicit through model, has_view_permission(request, obj) returns True if the request.user has either the 'view' or the 'change' permission on the target model (the model other than parent_model that the through model relates to); it no longer grants add/change/delete via that view check.

When running the psql subprocess via runshell_db, if conn_params contains a truthy 'sslmode' value, the subprocess environment (passed as env= to subprocess.run) has its 'PGSSLMODE' variable set to str(sslmode); if the parameter is absent or falsey, 'PGSSLMODE' is not injected into the environment.

When trimming leading joins off the exclude subquery, a leading 'self'/base-table join may only be removed when the following join is not tied to a FilteredRelation; if that join originates from a FilteredRelation (an INNER join carrying one), it is kept so that the FilteredRelation's filter condition continues to apply inside the subquery.

The '--skip-checks' parser argument is added to a command's parser only when requires_system_checks is True; a command whose requires_system_checks is False does not gain a --skip-checks parser option (so its help output does not list the flag and the parser does not bind it).

The cached hostname exposed by django.core.mail.utils DNS_NAME (CachedDnsName) is returned in punycoded ASCII form: get_fqdn() returns punycode(socket.getfqdn()) and __str__() yields that same ASCII form, so a non-ASCII system hostname is rendered as its `xn--` ACE label while an ASCII hostname is returned unchanged.
EnumSerializer.serialize() returns the imports set {'import <module>'} for the enum member's module, without including any imports that serializing the member's underlying value would require.

During the same Model._check_ordering relation-path walk, once a path segment resolves to a field that is not a relation, the walk no longer treats any subsequent segment as a field of the model owned by the enclosing relation path (in the buggy code _cls kept that model and a later segment matching one of its real field names was silently accepted); a further segment after a non-relation field is now acceptable only if it resolves as a registered transform/lookup of that non-relation field, and if it cannot, that ordering entry produces an E015 error.

When resolve_lookup_value is given a list/tuple whose elements are themselves lists/tuples, the nested iterables are resolved recursively and each nested level likewise preserves its own container type (list stays list, tuple stays tuple) across all nesting depths, rather than only the outermost level being handled.

During model setup for a subclass with parents but no declared explicit primary key, promoting the selected parent field to be the model's primary key no longer raises ImproperlyConfigured('Add parent_link=True to <field>.') when that field's remote_field.parent_link is not True.

Query.output_field, when len(self.select) == 1 and the single select expression exposes a 'target' attribute that is truthy (e.g. a Col selecting a concrete column), returns that element's 'target' field rather than the element's own 'field'/output field.

When alter_index_together removes an index_together grouping (an entry in the old set not present in the new), the schema editor locates for deletion only a constraint whose introspection reports index=True and unique=False for those columns, i.e. a plain (non-unique) index; a unique constraint spanning the very same columns is excluded from the deletion lookup so that it is not deleted and the removal does not fail with a "Found wrong number..." ValueError merely because that unique constraint exists.

ExpressionWrapper.get_group_by_cols(alias=None) delegates transparently to its wrapped inner expression, returning self.expression.get_group_by_cols(alias=alias). As a result, when an ExpressionWrapper is included in GROUP BY processing it contributes exactly the GROUP BY columns that its wrapped inner expression contributes (e.g. none when the inner expression is a bare constant Value, because Value.get_group_by_cols() returns []), rather than the wrapper expression node itself being treated as a GROUP BY column.

Query.clone() (invoked whenever a QuerySet is chained/cloned, including the clone QuerySet.none() makes before it sets the query empty) produces independent clones of each of the source query's combined_queries sub-query objects rather than sharing references to them, so that mutating a clone's combined sub-queries (e.g. recursively emptying them via set_empty) does not alter the source combined queryset's constituent sub-queries.

When FileExtensionValidator rejects an upload whose extension is not allowed, the ValidationError it raises carries the rejected file value in params under 'value', in addition to its existing 'extension' and 'allowed_extensions' keys.

When display_for_field is called with a value that is truthy and a field that is a models.JSONField, the returned text is the JSON serialization of that value in which non-ASCII characters appear as literal characters rather than as \uXXXX escapes (serialized with python json.dumps using ensure_ascii=False and the field's encoder); on a serialization TypeError it still falls back to display_for_value(value, empty_value_display).

Frame generation for each contributing exception skips traceback frames whose frame locals set __traceback_hide__ to a truthy value, and otherwise reports every frame of that exception's traceback in tb_next order; the last reported frame of the whole list corresponds to the last non-hidden frame reached.

When `__main__.__spec__` is None or its `parent` is falsy (i.e. the process was not launched as a package via `-m`), get_child_arguments() does not add any ['-m', ...] entry and instead falls through to script-path handling: it returns [str(<sys.argv[0] with .exe suffix>)] + sys.argv[1:] if that .exe exists, [sys.executable] + warning options + [str(<sys.argv[0] with '-script.py' suffix>)] + sys.argv[1:] if that script exists, appends full sys.argv (including argv[0]) when sys.argv[0] exists, and raises RuntimeError('Script %s does not exist.' % sys.argv[0]) when sys.argv[0] does not exist.

ThreadedWSGIServer's __init__ accepts an optional keyword argument connections_override (defaulting to None) and stores the passed value unchanged on the instance as the attribute connections_override.

Q.deconstruct() no longer special-cases a single non-Q child by re-encoding it into keyword kwargs: for a Q built from a single lookup keyword (single two-element child, e.g. Q(name='x')), the child is now returned as an element of the positional args (args=(('name','x'),)) with an empty kwargs dict, rather than as args=() with kwargs={'name':'x'}.

URLValidator raises a ValidationError (message 'Enter a valid URL.', code 'invalid', params {'value': value}) when the value is a str that contains any tab ('\t'), carriage-return ('\r'), or line-feed ('\n') character, and this rejection happens even when the same value would otherwise have been accepted by the trivial regex or by the IDN retry path.

BoundWidget.id_for_label returns the value of the 'id' key in the subwidget's data['attrs'] dictionary, i.e. the id attribute that will actually be rendered on that option/input; when data['attrs'] contains no 'id' entry (e.g. the form has auto_id disabled and the widget's own attrs specify no id), it returns None rather than fabricating an id string from the widget name and index.
QuerySet.bulk_update() called with an empty collection of objects (objs with no elements, after all field/pk validation has passed) returns the integer 0 rather than returning None.

modelformset_factory(model, ...) accepts an `edit_only` keyword argument that defaults to False, and the FormSet class it returns exposes a class attribute `edit_only` whose value equals the `edit_only` argument passed in.
django.utils.timezone._get_timezone_name(tz) returns the result of tz.tzname(None) when that call yields a truthy (non-None, non-empty) string, and otherwise falls back to returning str(tz).

When migrate() is invoked with an explicit empty plan (plan == []) and the django_migrations table does not exist on the migration connection's database, migrate() returns the ProjectState built from the unmigrated apps (with_applied_migrations=False) without creating the django_migrations table (i.e. it performs an early return before ensure_schema/table creation and before folding applied migrations into the state).

When the schema editor removes a unique_together (deleted set in alter_unique_together processed through _delete_composed_index), it locates the database constraint to drop by filtering to constraints that are unique and are NOT primary keys. As a result, for a model whose removed unique_together field set is also (or includes) the primary key on a backend whose introspection reports that primary-key constraint as unique=True, the removal no longer counts the primary key as one of the matching unique constraints and therefore no longer raises "Found wrong number (...)"; it drops only the actual unique constraint and leaves the primary key intact.

A ModelForm subclass whose Meta class declares a formfield_callback has that callback applied when constructing that form's model-derived fields: each model field is routed through the Meta's callback rather than the default f.formfield() building.

When ServerHandler processes a HEAD request and the WSGI application's response set a Content-Length header, that Content-Length header is removed before the response is finalized, so the HEAD response does not advertise a body length derived from the (stripped) payload.

In _ImageBase._make_image, when norming resampled 2D image data whose norm is a LogNorm, if the recomputed/un-scaled vmin (s_vmin) is less than or equal to 0, that vmin is set to np.finfo(scaled_dtype).eps (the smallest representable positive float of the scaled dtype) before the norm is invoked, so that the norm is never handed a vmin of 0 or negative. Consequently a render whose round-tripped vmin is exactly 0 succeeds (the previous code only corrected strictly negative vmin and would pass vmin==0 through, causing the log-norm application to fail on that boundary).
Constructing a Legend whose parent is neither an Axes nor a FigureBase raises TypeError with the exact message 'Legend needs either Axes or FigureBase as parent'.

When drawedges=True on a filled Colorbar that has no lower extension (_extend_lower() false), no divider is drawn at the lower vmin extreme — dividers there are only drawn if such a lower extension exists; likewise _extend_lower()/start_idx still starts cutting the interior below the lowest interior box boundary when no lower extension is present.

In ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks, when the finest tick level whose values vary across the given ticks is at the year (level 0) or month (level 1) field, the offset is now forcibly suppressed (so no offset string is shown/offset_string stays empty) only if the set of distinct values taken by that field across the ticks includes the value 1 (e.g., a January tick when months vary); when those varying values do not include 1, the offset is kept displayed (show_offset stays on) even though the varying level is a year/month level.

Colormap.__call__ converts a non-float input X (an array whose dtype kind is not 'f', e.g. integer/unsigned/bool kinds) into a native signed integer dtype before substituting the over-range (self._i_over), under-range (self._i_under), and bad (self._i_bad) sentinel indices, so those substitutions always act on a signed buffer large enough to hold values self.N, self.N+1, and self.N+2. As a result, invoking a colormap on such an input -- including on an empty array such as np.array([], dtype=np.uint8), for which the sentinel indices self.N+2, self.N+1, self.N exceed the uint8 range when self.N=256 -- completes without emitting NumPy conversion/out-of-bounds (deprecation) warnings.

For a DraggableBase instance d, d.canvas returns the canvas of d.ref_artist.figure (i.e. d.ref_artist.figure.canvas), resolved dynamically at access time rather than captured once at construction, so that .canvas still evaluates correctly (resolving to the re-attached figure's canvas) after the helper has been unpickled and re-attached to a figure; reads of self.canvas used for supports_blit checks, callback (dis)connection and canvas redraw/blit continue to work.
A Grouper instance whose _mapping holds weak references to live, weak-referenceable objects can be pickled (and unpickled, e.g. via pickle/copy.deepcopy) without raising an error.

Calling twinx() on an Axes whose x-axis has units set returns a new twin Axes whose xaxis.units equals the calling Axes' self.xaxis.units (i.e. the parent x-axis unit configuration is carried onto the shared horizontal axis of the returned twin).
When prepare_content_length is called with body=None on a request whose method is neither 'GET' nor 'HEAD' (e.g. POST), the 'Content-Length' header is still set to '0'.

PandasIndexAdapter exposes a new copy(deep=True) method that returns a new PandasIndexAdapter; with deep=True it wraps a deep copy of the underlying pandas index, with deep=False it shares the same underlying index, and in both cases the adapter's stored dtype is preserved on the returned adapter.

In the dot (.dot) class diagram emitted by DotWriter.get_values / write_classes, each displayed method whose signature declares a type annotation on a positional argument other than `self` is rendered with that annotation as `methodname(argname: Type)`, pairing each annotation to its argument positionally; arguments without an annotation are rendered bare `argname` (multiple arguments joined by ', ').

When the PYLINTHOME environment variable is not set, the home directory resolves to a real path (USER_HOME is not "~"), and the legacy directory os.path.join(USER_HOME, ".pylint.d") already exists on disk, importing pylint.config prints a message to stderr stating that PYLINTHOME is now the new cache directory while the obsolescent old .pylint.d directory was found and can be safely removed (this is an existence check only — it does not create or delete the old directory).

Calling Similar.run() on an instance whose min_lines equals 0 returns immediately and does no similarity computation and produces no similarity report output on stdout (neither computed duplicates nor the TOTAL-lines summary line). Positive min_lines values still compute and display the report as before.
Given a list or tuple, pylint.utils._check_regexp_csv yields each element exactly as provided, without splitting, stripping, or otherwise transforming the elements.

Under `--pdb`, TestCaseFunction.runtest() suppresses the deferred-tearDown mechanism (which postpones the unittest tearDown until pytest teardown and replaces the testcase's tearDown with a no-op) only when the currently running test is not skipped — now treating a class-level `@unittest.skip` (i.e. __unittest_skip__ set on the enclosing test class) as skipped, so that for a skipped whole class the testcase's real tearDown is left intact and runs normally rather than being deferred/replaced.

fowlkes_mallows_score returns a correct Fowlkes-Mallows score (a value in the expected range, not corrupted by integer overflow) even when the contingency counts are large enough that the product of the two squared row/column sums (pk·qk) would exceed the range of a signed 64-bit integer; specifically the returned value is computed without ever forming that overflowing product.

The function sklearn.decomposition.dict_learning() accepts a new keyword `method_max_iter` (default 1000) that is propagated as the `max_iter` of the sparse_encoding lasso solve performed in each dictionary-update step.

When data_to_wrap is already a pandas DataFrame, _wrap_in_pandas_container ignores the index argument and preserves the input DataFrame's own existing index; it never reassigns data_to_wrap.index from the index parameter for DataFrame inputs. Consequently it does not raise a pandas 'Length mismatch' ValueError even when the supplied index is shorter/different in length from the DataFrame's rows. (Columns are still assigned in place when the columns argument is not None.)

IsolationForest.score_samples still behaves as before for external callers: it validates the user-supplied X (accepting/ converting to float32 csr via _validate_data with reset=False) and returns the negation of the per-sample averaged anomaly scores, delegating the fitted-state check and scoring computation to an internal method that does not re-run input validation (so calling score_samples on an already-fitted DataFrame still yields the expected scores).

SequentialFeatureSelector.fit determines the cross-validation splitting strategy once using a classifier-aware check (classifier=True when the wrapped estimator is a classifier and False otherwise), so any cross-validation-driven validation that depends on classifier vs regressor semantics is resolved identically for all fold usages throughout a single fit.

The n_init candidate runs of k_means are each initialized from an independent per-run random seed (each run receiving its own fresh RandomState seeded by one element of a pre-sampled seed array drawn from the caller's random_state at the start), rather than from a single shared advancing random stream whose state depends on the sequential execution path, so each of the n_init runs' initialization outcome is the same regardless of whether the calling path is single-job or parallel.
sphinx.pycode.ast.unparse() on an AST Tuple node whose elts list is empty returns the string '()' rather than the empty string that would result from joining zero element strings.

When rendering a C++ signature, a user-defined-literal's literal operator suffix identifier is shown as a (non-emphasised) plain text piece linked through a pending cross-reference whose reftarget is the literal-operator name `operator""IDENT`; correspondingly the description mode string 'udl' becomes acceptable to verify_description_mode so ASTIdentifier.describe_signature can be invoked in that mode.

When linkcheck checks a URL with a fragment anchor (anchor present, not ignored, and linkcheck_anchors enabled) and the streamed GET of the anchor's base URL (req_url) returns an HTTP error status, the URL is reported based on that HTTP error via the standard status handling (401 as 'working'/'- unauthorized', 503 as 'ignored' with the error, any other error status as 'broken' with the error) rather than being reported as 'Anchor ... not found' after scanning the error document body.

In DocFieldTransformer.transform, when an otherwise-unknown/argument-mismatched typed field is still re-linked from its single-node text content, the resulting xref is now generated with the document's BuildEnvironment passed through, so that this fallback path applies the same domain field-xref processing and scope (py:module/py:class) as the standard doc-field xref path instead of producing an env-less xref.

sphinx.ext.viewcode.collect_pages yields no viewcode pages (no per-module highlighted source pages and no '_modules/index' overview page) when the active builder is the singlehtml builder (builder.name == 'singlehtml').

The '|' delimiter, together with any whitespace surrounding it, is preserved in the rendered output as plain non-reference content between the per-alternative references, rather than being dropped or folded into the reftarget of either neighboring type reference.
For any non-empty input x, is_path_or_empty(x) validates x exactly as is_path does: it returns the (tilde-expanded) path if x resolves to an existing directory, and raises ValidationError otherwise.

Mock classes carry an explicit class-level __name__: a bare _MockObject instance exposes __name__ == '' (H0), while every subclass manufactured by _make_subclass (as returned by e.g. __getattr__/__getitem__ attribute access on a mock module or object, and used when a mocked class is used as a base) exposes __name__ equal to that member/attribute name (H2). Reading __name__ on a mock thus yields a real string value rather than falling back into __getattr__ and returning another mock.

Identity._entry(i, j) returns the KroneckerDelta(i, j) expression (left unevaluated) rather than a concrete scalar when Eq(i, j) evaluates to neither the boolean True object nor the boolean False object — i.e. when the indices are distinct symbolic/index expressions whose equality is not statically decidable (e.g. two independent symbols that could still be equal in value).

When an object that is already an instance of the requested class is passed to the constructor with an explicit size different from its own, the result is a new instance of that same class (subclass preserved) resized to the given size.

When Product._eval_product is applied to a term that is an Add whose as_numer_denom() yields a purely numeric (is_Number) denominator q — i.e. the term cannot be factored into independently-evaluable numerator/denominator products, such as n + 2**(-k) or n**(2/3) + 1 — the returned value is exp(Sum(log(p), (k, a, n))) / q (p being the numerator), rather than the sum over the separately-evaluated products of the numerator's individual Add addends.

When mul_symbol is a custom string whose content is whitespace/empty once stripped, or is one of the LaTeX spacing commands r'\,', r'\:', r'\;', r'\quad', or a lone backslash r'\', the number-separator used when printing floats (mantissa-exponent form) and between adjacent numeric terms is the dot symbol (r' \cdot ') rather than the literal custom string.

MpmathPrinter renders the integer numerator e.p and denominator e.q of a Rational directly into the emitted code (interpolated verbatim, including the sign of a negative numerator such as Rational(-3,2) being rendered as mpmath.mpf(-3)/mpmath.mpf(2)), so rational values of arbitrary size and either sign are represented losslessly in the generated expression rather than approximated or pre-evaluated at print/parse time.

For a symbol in MathMLPresentationPrinter._print_Symbol whose name decomposes into a base identifier plus subscript(s) and/or superscript(s) (e.g. Symbol('x2') -> base 'x', subscript '2'), the printed top-level element for that symbol is the structural element itself (an <msub> when only a subscript is present, an <msup> when only a superscript is present, or an <msubsup> when both are present), containing the base <mi> and the script content -- the structural element is no longer nested inside an outer <mi> wrapper.

After the removal step triggered by a newly found minimal block system, the set of block systems retained for comparison against subsequent candidates (and ultimately returned) is exactly the previously recorded systems that were not subsumed by the new candidate, so all systems rendered non-minimal (not merely the first one encountered) are dropped and none is dropped spuriously.

Expression.__bool__ (truthiness of an EX ring element) returns falsy (False) whenever the wrapped SymPy expression f.ex is definitively zero, i.e. f.ex.is_zero is True, even when f.ex is not structurally equal to the Python integer 0; it returns truthy (True) in every other case (definitive nonzero or undecidable zero-ness).

Equality/identity evaluation between two generic Set instances (the multiple-dispatch _eval_is_eq rule matched when neither operand has a more-specific handler) is determined by mutual subsethood: it resolves to (the fuzzy logic of) whether lhs.is_subset(rhs) AND rhs.is_subset(lhs) are both true, in place of the previous blanket 'None' answer that left such equalities unevaluated.

Float.__eq__ returns Python False when the right operand sympifies to a Boolean (S.false/S.true, or Python bool False/True via _sympify), regardless of the Float's value — in particular a zero-valued Float no longer short-circuits through 'not other' and so no longer compares equal to S.false.

Mod.eval no longer propagates a PolynomialError raised by the internal gcd(p, q)/gcd_terms simplification step: when gcd(p, q) on the dividend/divisor arguments raises PolynomialError (e.g. piecewise-related generator issue), evaluation catches it, treats the extracted common factor G as 1 so that no gcd reduction is applied, and continues with the remainder of the Mod.eval simplification, ultimately returning a valid Mod result (an evaluated result or an unevaluated Mod form) instead of raising.

AntiSymmetricTensor._latex renders as a brace-group enclosing the whole symbol with both its upper and lower indices, i.e. it returns '{%s^{%s}_{%s}}' formatting '{symbol^{upper}_{lower}}' rather than 'symbol^{upper}_{lower}'.

In CodePrinter._print_Mul, when an expression has a clearly-negative leading coefficient (sign '-') and its numerator reduces to exactly one factor, that lone factor is parenthesized against a weight strictly between PRECEDENCE['Mul'] and PRECEDENCE['Pow'] (0.5*(PRECEDENCE['Pow']+PRECEDENCE['Mul'])) rather than against the (Add-level) precedence of the negative Mul itself; consequently such a lone factor whose own precedence is below Pow-level (e.g. a Mul-level object) is now emitted inside parentheses directly after the leading '-'.

String is now a subclass of sympy.core.expr.Atom (in addition to Token), so every String instance (and its subclasses QuotedString and Comment) is an instance of Atom and exhibits SymPy atomic semantics (e.g. treated as an atom rather than a container by Basic traversal operations).

When PythonCodePrinter (and its subclass MpmathPrinter, both built atop AbstractPythonCodePrinter) prints a Min expression, the result is a call to the Python builtin min with the Min's arguments as comma-separated operands (i.e. code string of form `min(...)`), instead of the previous rewrite-to-Piecewise/`# Not supported` fallback.

The plain (non-mod-D) ZZ Hermite-normal-form computation steps through all rows of the matrix from bottom to top, not merely the bottom min(m, n) rows, and stops only once a pivot occupies every one of the n columns. Consequently, for an integer matrix with more rows than columns (m > n) whose genuinely nonzero row(s) lie above the bottom min(m, n) rows, the returned HNF keeps columns holding nonzero pivots obtained from those upper rows rather than returning a column-stripped (empty-column) result that discards them; e.g. hermite_normal_form of a ZZ matrix such as [[2,7],[0,0],[0,0]] returns a result retaining the top row's pivot column instead of an empty 3x0 result.
Contains(x, S).as_set() returns S (the set given as the second argument of the Contains) instead of raising NotImplementedError.

When checking a candidate homomorphism whose domain is a PermutationGroup, a presentation relator word containing terms with negative powers (inverses of generators) is evaluated and contributes toward the identity check: each relator term's free-generator symbol maps to the corresponding domain generator and is raised to that term's (possibly negative) power in the accumulated image, so such relators are no longer skipped.
